## Architecture Diagrams

Dock card updates:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Swift DockStore
  participant R as Dock relay
  participant S as Relay SQLite
  participant H as Raw app-server history
  participant L as Raw app-server live endpoints

  C->>R: initialize / initialized
  C->>R: dock/subscribe
  R->>R: install subscriber and buffer newer updates
  R->>S: read snapshot
  R-->>C: snapshot
  loop boot/periodic/forced reconcile
    R->>L: thread/loaded/list + thread/read
    R->>H: thread/list + thread/read
    R->>H: thread/turns/list for activity proof
    R->>S: write cards, freshness, completeness, seq
    R-->>C: dock/update
  end
  C->>R: dock/resync on schema/epoch/seq/window gap
  R-->>C: replacement snapshot
```

Thread Detail updates:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Swift ThreadDetailStore
  participant R as Dock relay
  participant H as Raw app-server history/live route
  participant U as Raw live upstream session

  C->>R: initialize / initialized
  C->>R: thread/read includeTurns:false
  R->>H: route to live row or history
  H-->>R: compact metadata
  R-->>C: metadata
  loop all pages
    C->>R: thread/turns/list sortDirection:desc
    R->>H: live endpoint or history endpoint
    H-->>R: page
    R-->>C: page
  end
  C->>R: thread/resume excludeTurns:true
  R->>U: initialize + thread/resume
  U-->>R: live notifications / server requests
  R-->>C: forwarded JSON-RPC notifications / requests
```

The dangerous detail failure:

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Swift detail WS
  participant R as Relay downstream session
  participant U as Upstream app-server WS

  C->>R: thread/resume
  R->>U: upstream thread/resume
  U-->>R: live notifications
  U--xR: upstream closes
  R->>U: retry initialize + thread/resume
  U-->>R: recovery succeeds
  Note over C,R: Phone WebSocket never closed, so Swift sees no reconnect.
  Note over C: Swift does not re-run thread/read + thread/turns/list.
```

### Initialization

- `initialize`
  - Client sends client identity/capability metadata.
  - Default Swift identity is `name:"codex_dock"`, title `Codex Dock`, version
    `0.1.0`.
  - Default capabilities set `experimentalApi:true`,
    `requestAttestation:false`, and no `optOutNotificationMethods`.
  - Relay returns relay metadata including `relayInstanceID`.
  - Code: `AppServerClient.connectAndInitialize` in
    `CodexDock/AppServer/AppServerClient.swift:206`.
  - Relay handler: `scripts/dock-relay.mjs:448`.

- `initialized`
  - Client sends this notification after `initialize`.
  - Used as JSON-RPC session handshake completion.
  - Current relay behavior ignores downstream notifications with no id, while
    diagnostics code still models `initialized` as a passive route. That is a
    diagnostics drift point.

### Dock Card Stream

- `dock/subscribe`
  - Client asks for the initial Dock snapshot.
  - Relay subscribes the downstream connection to future `dock/update`
    notifications and returns a snapshot.
  - Swift call: `AppServerThreadCardStreamConnection.subscribe` in
    `CodexDock/State/AppServerThreadCardStreamClient.swift:95`.
  - Relay route: `scripts/dock-relay.mjs:458`.

- `dock/update`
  - Relay notification carrying a Dock delta, snapshot fallback, or heartbeat.
  - Swift listens to notifications and decodes only this route for Dock:
    `CodexDock/State/AppServerThreadCardStreamClient.swift:65`.
  - Relay publishes deltas through
    `scripts/dock-relay-state-subscriptions.mjs:112`.

- `dock/resync`
  - Client asks for a replacement Dock snapshot when sequence, schema, view,
    epoch, or window validation fails.
  - Swift calls it from `DockStore.resync` in
    `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift:323`.
  - Relay route: `scripts/dock-relay.mjs:460`.

### Archive Card Stream

- `archive/subscribe`
  - Client asks for initial Archive snapshot.
  - Relay subscribes the downstream connection to future `archive/update`.
  - Swift uses the same `AppServerThreadCardStreamClient`, configured for
    `.archive`.

- `archive/update`
  - Relay notification carrying Archive changes.

- `archive/resync`
  - Client asks for replacement Archive snapshot.

Important distinction: Dock Home keeps a long-lived stream. Archive loading in
the current Swift path is mostly one-shot snapshot collection, not a persistent
visible Archive stream.

### Thread Detail

- `thread/read`
  - Client reads thread metadata with `includeTurns:false`.
  - Relay routes to live endpoint if the thread is live, otherwise history.
  - Swift call: `ThreadDetailStore.readFullThread` in
    `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:563`.
  - Relay route: `scripts/dock-relay.mjs:466`.

- `thread/turns/list`
  - Client drains all historical turns page by page.
  - Swift sends `sortDirection:.desc` and detects repeated cursors.
  - Swift call: `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:581`.
  - Relay route: `scripts/dock-relay.mjs:468`.

- `thread/resume`
  - Client asks relay to create a live upstream session for one thread.
  - Relay forces `excludeTurns:true`.
  - Relay validates human thread identity, opens upstream app-server WebSocket,
    initializes it, calls upstream `thread/resume`, then forwards live
    notifications/requests.
  - Swift call: `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:611`.
  - Relay route: `scripts/dock-relay.mjs:470`.

### Thread Commands

- `turn/start`
  - Sent when the phone composer has no active in-progress turn.
  - Relay only forwards it after a matching `thread/resume` on the same
    downstream connection.

- `turn/steer`
  - Sent when there is an active in-progress turn.
  - Relay checks the request `threadId` matches the bound resumed thread.

- `turn/interrupt`
  - Relay supports forwarding it.
  - Swift has the constant, but no public wrapper equivalent to
    `turnStart`/`turnSteer` in the currently audited code.

### Composer Command Path

Swift composer sending is intentionally tiny, and that is the right shape:

1. `ThreadDetailStore.sendComposerDraft` checks the detail session exists.
2. It rejects sends while voice dictation is busy.
3. It trims the draft and no-ops empty text.
4. It marks `composer.isSending = true`.
5. It calls `ClientCommandEngine.sendDraft`.
6. `ClientCommandEngine` chooses:
   - `turn/steer` when `activeTurnID` is non-nil;
   - `turn/start` when `activeTurnID` is nil.
7. `turn/start` and `turn/steer` both use a single text input object:
   `{ type:"text", text, text_elements:[] }`.
8. On success, Swift clears the draft and sets `activeTurnID` to the returned
   turn id if present.
9. On failure, Swift preserves the draft and shows the error.

Active turn tracking:

- Historical active turn id comes from any turn whose `status` is
  `inProgress`; the last one wins.
- Live `turn/started` notification sets `activeTurnID`.
- Live `turn/completed` clears it only if the completed turn id matches the
  current active turn id.

Relay command gate:

- `turn/start`, `turn/steer`, and `turn/interrupt` are not history routes.
- They require the same downstream socket to have successfully completed
  `thread/resume`.
- They require the request `threadId` to match the resumed thread.
- They require `acceptedHumanThreadId` to match, proving the route was not
  opened against automation/internal work.

### Server Requests

Server requests are JSON-RPC requests sent by app-server, through the relay, to
the phone. They are not normal notifications.

- Relay forwards upstream server requests in `scripts/dock-relay.mjs:321`.
- Swift receives them from `AppServerClient.serverRequests`.
- Thread Detail turns them into request cards in
  `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:766`.
- The phone answers with a JSON-RPC response using the original request id.
- Stale downstream responses are rejected if the relay no longer has a matching
  active upstream request.

Known request-card methods in Swift:

- `item/commandExecution/requestApproval`: command approval card; phone can
  accept or decline.
- `item/fileChange/requestApproval`: file-change approval card; phone can
  accept or decline.
- `item/permissions/requestApproval`: permissions approval card; phone can
  grant or decline turn-scoped permissions.
- `item/tool/requestUserInput`: user-input card; phone can submit an answer.
- `mcpServer/elicitation/request`: MCP elicitation card; phone can currently
  decline, but not submit content.
- everything else: visible as unsupported "Needs desktop".

Relay request safety:

- forwarded server requests are recorded with request id, generation, method,
  and thread id when available;
- phone responses are forwarded only when the id belongs to the current relay
  downstream session generation;
- unknown or stale response ids get `no matching active upstream request`;
- responses fail if there is no active upstream session.

Swift request-card caveat: `serverRequest/resolved` handling is thin and can be
lost when the notification lacks a matching `threadId`, because Thread Detail
drops notifications not associated with the expected thread.

### Realtime Transcription

The phone speaks to relay-owned transcription routes:

- `audio/transcription/start`
- `audio/transcription/append`
- `audio/transcription/commit`
- `audio/transcription/cancel`
- `audio/transcription/delta`
- `audio/transcription/completed`
- `audio/transcription/failed`
- `audio/transcription/canceled`
- `audio/transcription/closed`

The relay forbids phone-supplied provider configuration. Model, delay, and
provider selection are relay-side.

End-to-end transcription flow:

1. Swift opens or retains a relay WebSocket through `AppServerHostConnector`.
2. Swift sends `audio/transcription/start`.
3. Relay `RealtimeTranscriptionManager` rejects phone-supplied provider config,
   checks that no transcription session is already active on that downstream
   relay session, and requires `openAIAPIKey` on the relay.
4. Relay opens an OpenAI Realtime transcription WebSocket using relay-side
   model/endpoint/language/delay settings.
5. Relay returns `{ sessionId, format:"audio/pcm", sampleRate, model, language,
   delay }`.
6. Swift sends monotonic `audio/transcription/append` chunks with base64 PCM
   audio.
7. Relay validates monotonic sequence, chunk size, pending bytes, and basic
   audio stats, then forwards `input_audio_buffer.append` upstream.
8. Swift sends `audio/transcription/commit` to commit the upstream input audio
   buffer, or `audio/transcription/cancel` to cancel.
9. Relay converts upstream transcription deltas/completions into downstream
   notifications:
   - `audio/transcription/delta`;
   - `audio/transcription/completed`;
   - `audio/transcription/failed`;
   - `audio/transcription/canceled`;
   - `audio/transcription/closed`.
10. Relay closes the active transcription session on completion, cancellation,
    failure, max duration, or downstream close.

Transcription is independent of Dock cards and Thread Detail events. It shares
the downstream relay session object, but it is not a raw app-server route and it
does not use the Dock card stream or `thread/resume` upstream.

### Archive Mutations

- `thread/archive`
- `thread/unarchive`

The relay executes the mutation and then asks the state engine to reconcile.
Current audit finding: the mutation path is mechanically wrong for Archive
subscribers:

```text
thread/archive or thread/unarchive
  -> relayStateEngine.handleArchiveMutation
  -> NotificationIngestor.ingestArchiveMutation
  -> scheduleReconciliation({ reason, immediate:true })
  -> StateReconciler.run
  -> RelayStateEngine.reconcileDock
```

`reconcileArchive` is not called from this mutation chain. It currently runs
after `archive/subscribe` and `archive/resync` via
`scheduleArchiveReconciliationAfterResponse`. Therefore a fix that merely
"schedules reconciliation" can still be wrong; the Archive view must explicitly
schedule or run Archive reconciliation so `archive/update` subscribers get the
mutation result.

### Diagnostics HTTP Routes

Relay exposes:

- `/readyz`
- `/healthz`
- `/statusz`
- `/metricsz`
- `/routesz`
- `/syncz`

These prove process or route health, not semantic data freshness. A stale or
partial `dock/subscribe` response can still be counted as a successful route
response.

Current diagnostics caveats:

- `/syncz` currently reports `state:"available"` without checking SQLite
  health, sync scopes, stale freshness, or reconciliation failures.
- The relay runtime snapshot exposes `relayStateHealth`, but status/metrics
  code paths have evidence of reading `runtime.relayState` instead. Exact
  current anchors:
  - `scripts/dock-relay.mjs:554` builds runtime state and
    `scripts/dock-relay.mjs:561` names it `relayStateHealth`;
  - `scripts/dock-relay-status.mjs:246` reads `runtime.relayState`;
  - `scripts/dock-relay-status.mjs:280` reads `runtime.relayState?.counts`;
  - `scripts/dock-relay-status.mjs:305` reads `runtime.relayState`.
  This can drop relay-state health from `/statusz`, `/metricsz`, or debug
  snapshots.
- Passive state stream notifications such as `dock/update` and `archive/update`
  are not recorded as route-health successes the way realtime transcription
  notifications are.

## App-Server Assumptions

The relay assumes the raw Codex app-server provides at least these behaviors.

### History APIs

- `thread/list` returns historical rows with pagination.
- `thread/read` can read thread metadata and optionally turns.
- `thread/turns/list` can page through the full turn history.
- Repeated cursors are a protocol error. Relay detects this for `thread/list`
  and `thread/turns/list`; Swift detects it in detail turn pagination.

Important: the relay no longer treats raw `thread/list` as enough for Dock card
recency. It uses `thread/list` as input, then proves each row's activity by
reading turns.

### Live APIs

- `thread/loaded/list` returns currently loaded/live thread ids.
- `thread/read includeTurns:false` can read each loaded thread for live status.
- `thread/resume excludeTurns:true` starts a live session for detail.
- Live sessions send notifications and server requests after resume.

If live endpoint probing fails, the relay currently counts failed live
endpoints, but the audited `refreshLiveLeases` path does not appear to make
that failure degrade Dock reconcile completeness. History proof can still look
complete while live status is degraded.

### Compaction

The app-server may return compact thread metadata from `thread/resume`. That is
why Thread Detail must first drain historical turns via `thread/turns/list` and
then replace the compact resume response's turns with the full turn list.

If this order is violated, detail can show only compact/latest data instead of
the full conversation.

### Status Meaning

Relay status mapping treats:

- active flags as the signal for needs approval, needs input, or running;
- raw idle as a normal status value, not necessarily "waiting for the user";
- not loaded as dormant;
- unknown status as decodable but not trusted for special behavior.

### Human-Started Filtering

The relay classifies and rejects subagent, exec, app-server/MCP, memory
consolidation, unknown, and contradictory origins before rows become Dock cards.
Swift still defensively filters non-human cards if malformed data reaches it.

The exact relay taxonomy lives in
`scripts/dock-relay-human-thread-filter.mjs`.

Accepted origins:

| Input signal | Accepted reason | Output fields |
| --- | --- | --- |
| normalized source `cli` | `human_cli` | `allowed:true`, `category:"human_started"`, `sourceKind:"human"` |
| normalized source `vscode` | `human_vscode` | same |
| custom source `atlas` | `human_custom_atlas` | same |
| custom source `chatgpt` | `human_custom_chatgpt` | same |

Rejected origins:

| Trigger | Reason | Source kind |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `source` contains `thread_spawn` / `threadSpawn` parent payload | `not_base_level` | `automation` |
| `threadSource` canonicalizes to `subagent` | `sub_agent` | `automation` |
| `threadSource` canonicalizes to `memoryconsolidation` | `memory_internal` | `internal` |
| `source` is missing, null, or empty | `missing_source` | `unknown` |
| normalized source `exec` | `exec` | `automation` |
| normalized source `appServer` without raw `mcp` signal | `app_server` | `automation` |
| normalized source `appServer` with raw `mcp` signal | `mcp` | `automation` |
| normalized source `subAgent` variant `threadSpawn` | `sub_agent_thread_spawn` | `automation` |
| normalized source `subAgent` other variants | `sub_agent` | `automation` |
| normalized source `internal` | `memory_internal` | `internal` |
| custom source not in `atlas`/`chatgpt` | `unknown` | `unknown` |
| unknown source with contradictory source families/kinds | `contradictory_source` | `unknown` |
| unknown source without contradictory signal | `unknown` | `unknown` |
| session-index supplement validates but archive scope does not match params | `archive_scope_mismatch` | local supplement rejection |

Relationship fields are derived at the same time:

- `relationship:"spawned"` if source contains thread-spawn parent metadata;
- `relationship:"forked"` if `forkedFromId` / `forked_from_id` exists;
- otherwise `relationship:"root"`;
- `parentThreadID` comes from thread-spawn metadata;
- `forkedFromID` comes from fork fields.

Materialization rule: only rows that become `lane:"human"` and
`sourceKind:"human"` survive the SQLite app-facing SQL filters used by Dock and
Archive. `deleteRejectedThreadCards` deletes stored rows outside that shape, and
`deleteRejectedLiveLeases` deletes live leases whose backing thread row is not
human-facing.

## Relay Upstream Mechanics

The relay has two upstream modes.

### History Client

`historyClientForConfig` owns the pooled history path:

- URL: `config.historyUrl`, defaulting to raw app-server
  `ws://127.0.0.1:4500`.
- Bearer: `config.historyBearerToken`.
- Pool: `UpstreamConnectionPool`.
- Initializer: `initializeClient`.

History is used for:

- `thread/list`;
- non-live `thread/read`;
- non-live `thread/turns/list`;
- `thread/unarchive`;
- `thread/archive` when the thread routes to history.

### Live Endpoints And Session Router

The relay also tracks live endpoints:

- `configuredLiveEndpointsForConfig` builds live endpoint records from
  `config.liveEndpoints`.
- Live endpoints can inherit `historyBearerToken` unless they provide their own
  bearer token.
- `LiveStatusCache` periodically reads loaded/live rows from these endpoints.
- `SessionRouter` chooses the endpoint for a thread:
  - live row source if the thread is loaded/live;
  - history endpoint otherwise.

This routing affects both Dock and Detail:

- Dock reconciliation merges live rows plus history rows.
- `thread/read` prefers a live row when available.
- `thread/turns/list` verifies the thread is human-started, then routes to live
  endpoint or history endpoint.
- `thread/resume` opens a dedicated upstream WebSocket to the routed endpoint.

1354	
1355	### Poll/Reconcile, Not Raw Push
1356	
1357	Dock card updates are not raw app-server push subscriptions. The relay builds
1358	card truth through reconciliation:
1359	
1360	1. poll live loaded rows;
1361	2. poll history `thread/list`;
1362	3. validate/enrich rows with `thread/read`;
1363	4. supplement from `session_index.jsonl`;
1364	5. prove newest activity with `thread/turns/list`;
1365	6. write SQLite;
1366	7. publish `dock/update`.

1368	Thread Detail live events are different: after `thread/resume`, the relay
1369	forwards raw upstream notifications and server requests from that dedicated
1370	upstream session.

1372	### Reconcile And Canonicalization Algorithm
1373	
1374	The relay card pipeline is not a flat `thread/list` passthrough. The canonical
1375	collapse points are `aggregateThreadList`, `canonicalizeThreadRows`,
1376	`normalizeThread`, and `RelayStateStore.applyDockReconciliation` /

1382	   `sourceKind` / `sourceKinds` and clamping `limit` to
1383	   `THREAD_LIST_MAX_LIMIT`.
1384	2. It calls history `thread/list`.
1385	3. It appends every row with `ordinal`, `pageIndex`, and `rowIndex`.
1386	4. It follows `nextCursor`.
1387	5. Repeated cursors mark the scope incomplete with an error.
1388	6. Thrown upstream errors mark the scope incomplete with an error.

1396	5. It preserves list `id`.
1397	6. It preserves the newest `createdAt`/`updatedAt` between list and read so
1398	   read metadata cannot downgrade the activity baseline.

1403

1645	  - keep existing label unless missing;
1646	  - keep existing rail unless missing;
1647	  - pin if either side is pinned;
1648	  - keep earliest `pinnedAt`;
1649	  - keep lowest `pinnedOrder`;
1650	  - normalize pinned order after merge.
1651	
1652	No production code may use local metadata as a card source. If a relay card is
1653	absent, local metadata must not render a row.

1655	### Host Identity Resolution Contract
1656	
1657	Three host ids can appear in the client:
1658	
1659	| Name | Source | Meaning |
1660	| --- | --- | --- |
1661	| Configured host id | `DockHostConfiguration.id` | The saved/launch endpoint entry Swift is using. |
1662	| Stream host id | `DockStreamHostDTO.id` | Host id emitted by the relay stream. |
1663	| Logical host id | `DockStreamHostDTO.logicalHostID` and `DockThreadCardDTO.logicalHostID` | Relay-owned stable host identity used in `HostScopedThreadID`. |
1664	
1665	`DockHostIdentityResolver` owns client-side alias resolution:
1666	
1667	1. Group observations by configured host id.
1668	2. For each configured host, choose the first observed logical host id from
1669	   stream hosts/cards; otherwise fall back to configured host id.
1670	3. Build aliases from:
1671	   - configured host id;
1672	   - configured display name;
1673	   - configured endpoint display string;
1674	   - observed stream host id;
1675	   - observed logical host id;
1676	   - observed display name;
1677	   - observed endpoint.
1678	4. Store exact aliases and lowercased normalized aliases.
1679	5. `logicalHostID(forAlias:sourceConfiguredHostID:)` returns:
1680	   - the source configured host's logical id when the source host is known and
1681	     the alias is empty/compatible with that source;
1682	   - a logical id only when the alias maps to exactly one logical host;
1683	   - nil for ambiguous aliases.
1684	6. `resolve(rowHostID:sourceConfiguredHostID:preferredConfiguredHostID:)`
1685	   chooses a configured host record in this order:
1686	   - source configured host id;
1687	   - preferred configured host id;
1688	   - a loaded/partial/empty host status;
1689	   - first record in registry order.
1690	7. `contains(rowHostID:sourceConfiguredHostID:in:)` requires the row alias to
1691	   resolve to the expected logical host id for that configured host.
1692	
1693	Why this matters:
1694	
1695	- Multi-endpoint setups can have multiple configured host entries that point at
1696	  the same relay logical host.
1697	- Rows use relay logical host ids, while settings/actions often need the
1698	  configured endpoint used to make the request.
1699	- A wrong alias match can make the UI look connected to one host while row
1700	  actions go to another configured endpoint.
1701	
1702	Hard rule: host aliasing can choose which configured endpoint owns an already
1703	delivered relay row. It must not create a row, merge rows from two logical
1704	hosts, or use endpoint aliases as card truth.

1706	## Dock Home End-To-End Flow
1707	
1708	1. Swift creates an `AppServerThreadCardStreamClient`.
1709	2. The stream client creates `AppServerClient(webSocketURL: relay, bearerToken:
1710	   nil, connectionPolicy: .liveDetail)`.
1711	3. Swift connects and sends `initialize`/`initialized`.
1712	4. `DockStore.openStream` calls `dock/subscribe`.
1713	5. Relay returns a snapshot from SQLite state.
1714	6. Relay's subscription code installs the subscriber before reading the
1715	   snapshot, buffers updates that arrive during snapshot creation, then sends
1716	   only buffered updates newer than the returned snapshot.
1717	7. Swift `ThreadCardTable.applySnapshot` validates schema, view, window, and
1718	   host/card policy.
1719	8. `DockStore.startUpdateTask` starts reading `dock/update`.
1720	9. Relay periodically reconciles app-server state:
1721	   - reads live rows from loaded sessions;
1722	   - reads history with `thread/list`;
1723	   - validates human-started rows with `thread/read`;
1724	   - adds session-index supplements;
1725	   - proves activity through `thread/turns/list`;
1726	   - writes card facts to SQLite;
1727	   - publishes `dock/update`.
1728	10. Swift `ThreadCardTable.applyUpdate` applies deltas if `baseSeq` matches,
1729	   otherwise requests `dock/resync`.
1730	11. `DockRenderProjector` converts accepted cards plus local metadata into
1731	    visible rows.
1732	12. `DockCardProjection` filters/searches/groups rows, but recency remains
1733	    relay-owned.

1750	### Dock Recovery Matrix
1751	
1752	This is the important recovery contract for the stale-Dock bug.
1753	
1754	| User/system action | Existing Swift connection? | Method called | Does it create a relay subscription? | What it can recover |
1755	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
1756	| Initial Dock load | No | `dock/subscribe` | Yes | Cold start, first snapshot, future `dock/update` notifications. |
1757	| Host added after reload | No connection for that host | `dock/subscribe` | Yes | New host stream. |
1758	| Pull/foreground/store `refresh()` with existing connection | Yes | `dock/resync` | No | Bad local table state, sequence/schema/window mismatch, stale snapshot if relay has newer SQLite. |
1759	| `synchronizeStreams()` after host list change | Existing valid host connection | `dock/resync` | No | Same as above. |
1760	| `synchronizeStreams()` after host removed | Removed host | close only | No | Cleanup. |
1761	| Stream update task throws or ends | Connection torn down | `openStream` -> `dock/subscribe` after delay | Yes | Broken downstream stream noticed by Swift. |
1762	| AppServerClient silently reconnects its WebSocket internally | Swift still holds same connection object | `initialize` only at transport layer | No | Transport reconnect only; it does not recreate `dock/subscribe`. |
1763	| Settings host connection test | Separate temporary connection | `dock/subscribe`, then close | Yes, but temporary | Proves one-shot route/snapshot only, not Dock Home stream freshness. |
1764	
1765	Net: `refresh()` is not a fix for a silently unsubscribed long-lived Dock stream.
1766	It sends `dock/resync` over the existing connection object. If the underlying
1767	`AppServerClient` transparently reconnected and the relay removed the old
1768	subscription on socket close, that existing connection object can be connected
1769	but unsubscribed. Only a full stream reopen with `dock/subscribe` recreates the
1770	relay subscription.

1772	### Archive Recovery Matrix
1773	
1774	Archive currently uses a collect-and-close path, not the long-lived Dock table.
1775	
1776	| User/system action | Connection shape | Method called | Continuity proof |
1777	| --- | --- | --- | --- |
1778	| Archive screen load | Ephemeral per-host stream | `archive/subscribe`, then updates until complete/terminal incomplete | Schema/view plus completion/freshness; no long-lived `epoch`/`baseSeq` table. |
1779	| Archive collector receives delta before complete | Same ephemeral stream | `archive/update` | Applies upsert/delete by id until completion. |
1780	| Archive collector times out or stream closes early | Same ephemeral stream | none | Fails host load; no resync loop. |
1781	| User restores/unarchives | Separate ephemeral command connection | `thread/unarchive` | Mutation request only; current relay schedules Dock reconcile, not Archive reconcile. |
1782	| User archives from Dock | Separate ephemeral command connection | `thread/archive` | Mutation request only; current relay schedules Dock reconcile, not Archive reconcile. |
1783	| `archive/resync` | Existing archive stream if caller has one | `archive/resync` | Relay schedules `reconcileArchive` after response; this path is not used by archive mutation ingest. |
1784	
1785	Net: Archive can be correct at one-shot load time and still miss mutation
1786	updates unless the Archive reconcile path is explicitly invoked. Archive does
1787	not have the same persistent recovery machinery as Dock Home.

1789	### Thread Detail Recovery Matrix
1790	
1791	Thread Detail recovery is tied to the downstream phone connection state, not
1792	the relay's hidden upstream state.
1793	
1794	| Event | Phone WebSocket state | Relay upstream state | Swift behavior | Gap |
1795	| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
1796	| Initial open | New downstream socket | New focused upstream after `thread/resume` | `thread/read`, drain `thread/turns/list`, `thread/resume`, publish, then replay buffered live events. | Good path. |
1797	| Downstream reconnect observed | Reconnecting -> connected; loaded; `liveState == .reconnecting` | New or resumed downstream connection | Re-run `thread/read`, drain turns, `thread/resume`, merge. | Good path if state transition is observed. |
1798	| Foreground resume while connected | Connected | Whatever relay currently has | Marks reconnecting and rehydrates. | Good manual/lifecycle path. |
1799	| Notification stream ends | Ended | Unknown | Mark stale. | User sees stale. |
1800	| Relay upstream closes and recovers | Phone socket remains open | New upstream created by relay retry | Swift sees no downstream reconnect and does not rehydrate. | Primary stale-detail bug. |
1801	| Relay upstream recovery fails | Phone socket closed by relay | Closed/error | Swift marks stale/error via stream/connection failure. | User sees failure. |
1802	
1803	Net: the missing proof is "relay upstream recovered but phone downstream did not
1804	rehydrate." That is not covered by fake reconnect tests that manually emit a
1805	downstream reconnect state.

1807	## Archive End-To-End Flow
1808	
1809	1. Swift Archive loading opens relay streams per host.
1810	2. It subscribes to `archive/subscribe`.
1811	3. It collects snapshots/updates until the Archive snapshot is complete or a
1812	   terminal partial state is reached.
1813	4. It projects archive rows for the Archive UI.
1814	5. Restore/unarchive calls `thread/unarchive`, then refreshes.
1815	
1816	Important current mismatch:
1817	
1818	- Archive loading is owned by `ThreadCardHostSnapshotLoader` and
1819	  `ThreadCardStreamSnapshotCollector`, not by `ThreadCardTable`.
1820	- The one-shot Archive collector validates schema/view, but it does not enforce
1821	  the same `epoch`, `baseSeq`, and `seq` continuity as `ThreadCardTable`.
1822	- Archive command reconciliation currently schedules `StateReconciler.run`,
1823	  which calls `reconcileDock`; it does not call `reconcileArchive`.
1824	- Freshness is host-global, so Dock and Archive can stale each other.
1825	- Archive mutation grace suppresses active re-adds briefly after a local archive
1826	  mark. If upstream archive propagation takes longer than the grace period, a
1827	  later complete active reconcile can allow a row to bounce back into active.

1829	## Thread Detail End-To-End Flow
1830	
1831	1. User opens a Dock row.
1832	2. Swift validates the row belongs to the selected host.
1833	3. Swift creates a detail session and connects to the relay.
1834	4. Swift sends `initialize`/`initialized`.
1835	5. Swift starts buffering live notifications and server requests.
1836	6. Swift calls `thread/read includeTurns:false`.
1837	7. Swift drains `thread/turns/list` until `nextCursor` is empty.
1838	8. Swift calls `thread/resume excludeTurns:true`.
1839	9. Swift replaces the compact resume response's turns with the drained turns.
1840	10. Swift publishes loaded detail state.
1841	11. Swift replays buffered live notifications/requests.
1842	12. Swift listens continuously for:
1843	    - JSON-RPC notifications;
1844	    - JSON-RPC server requests;
1845	    - connection state changes.

1944	## Update Model
1945	
1946	### Snapshot
1947	
1948	A snapshot is a full replacement for a card view. It carries:
1949	
1950	- `kind:"snapshot"`
1951	- `schemaVersion`
1952	- `view`
1953	- `epoch`
1954	- `seq`
1955	- `hosts`
1956	- `cards`
1957	- `complete`
1958	- `totalRows`
1959	- `window`
1960	- `freshness`
1961	
1962	Swift applies a compatible snapshot as the table state for that host/view.
1963	
1964	### Delta
1965	
1966	A delta is incremental. It carries:
1967	
1968	- `kind:"delta"`
1969	- `schemaVersion`
1970	- `view`
1971	- `epoch`
1972	- `baseSeq`
1973	- `seq`
1974	- optional host upserts;
1975	- card upserts;
1976	- card deletes;
1977	- optional `complete`, `totalRows`, `window`, and `freshness`.
1978	
1979	Swift requires `baseSeq == current seq` for normal deltas. If sequence, schema,
1980	view, epoch, or window contract is incompatible, Swift asks for `dock/resync`.
1981	
1982	### Heartbeat
1983	
1984	Swift accepts `kind:"heartbeat"` and can use it to mark freshness while keeping
1985	rows. The schema allows heartbeat, and Swift tests cover stale heartbeat
1986	retention.
1987	
1988	Current relay emission appears to be snapshot/delta only. The sync audit tool
1989	also treats only snapshot/delta as normal, which can drift from the Swift
1990	contract.
1991	
1992	### Epoch
1993	
1994	Epoch identifies a relay subscription generation. A delta for a different epoch
1995	requires resync.
1996	
1997	### Window
1998	
1999	Large card sets can be sent in windows. The initial snapshot can be partial,
2000	and catch-up window deltas can fill the rest.
2001	
2002	Current nuance: window catch-up deltas intentionally can use
2003	`baseSeq == seq == snapshot.seq`. Swift allows this so the window can complete
2004	without moving stream sequence.
2005	
2006	### Large Update Fallback
2007	
2008	If a relay delta is too large, the subscription hub can send a snapshot instead
2009	of a delta.
2010	
2011	### Window Catch-Up Restart
2012	
2013	When a snapshot is partial, the relay sends follow-up window deltas. If the
2014	store sequence changes during catch-up, the relay abandons that catch-up and
2015	sends a fresh restart snapshot for the same view.
2016	
2017	### Render Coalescing
2018	
2019	`DockScreenStore`, `ThreadDetailScreenStore`, and `ConnectivityScreenStore`
2020	submit render snapshots through `RenderCoalescer`. The coalescer is a UI-layer
2021	batching and revision guard:
2022	
2023	- it buffers newest snapshots according to `CodexDockConstants.Rendering`;
2024	- it drops older revisions after a newer revision is accepted;
2025	- it yields the accepted render snapshot to SwiftUI.
2026	
2027	It is not a protocol source of truth, not a cache of Codex work, and not a
2028	freshness oracle. It can hide intermediate paints, but it should not permanently
2029	hide the latest state if upstream updates keep arriving.
2030	
2031	## Relay State And Caches
2032	
2033	### SQLite
2034	
2035	The relay stores materialized card facts in
2036	`.codex-dock/relay-state.sqlite`. This is not the durable source of truth;
2037	Codex app-server history remains the durable source. SQLite is the relay's
2038	materialized cache for phone-safe card streams.
2039	
2040	This cache can create stale first impressions:
2041	
2042	- `dock/subscribe` can return what is currently in SQLite.
2043	- Reconciliation runs on boot/periodic triggers and after certain responses.
2044	- If the cache is old but still marked fresh/complete enough, the relay may
2045	  skip immediate reconciliation after response.
2046	- The relay SQLite cache assumes one real host identity per cache. Changing
2047	  `CODEX_DOCK_REAL_HOST_ID` prunes rows for other host ids.
2048	
2049	Relay store initialization:
2050	
2051	- opens `DatabaseSync`;
2052	- sets `PRAGMA journal_mode = WAL`;
2053	- sets `PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON`;
2054	- runs migrations;
2055	- prunes rows whose `host_id` does not match the configured host.

2119	  view reads.
2120	- `idx_changes_view_seq(view, seq)` supports stream delta lookup.
2121	
2122	Sequence model:
2123	
2124	- `currentSeq()` is `MAX(changes.seq)` or `0`.
2125	- Every reconcile writes a `changes` row and receives a new `seq`.
2126	- `dock/update` and `archive/update` use that value as stream sequence.
2127	- `stateGeneration` currently mirrors `seq`.
2128	- `pruneChanges` keeps only the newest `RELAY_STATE_CHANGE_RETENTION` changes.
2129	
2130	Pruning model:
2131	
2132	- `pruneForeignHosts` deletes non-current host rows from `hosts`, `threads`,
2133	  `sync_scopes`, `live_leases`, `conflicts`, `turn_cache`, `subscriptions`,
2134	  `changes`, and `audit_findings`.
2135	- This prevents one SQLite file from simultaneously serving multiple real host
2136	  identities, but it also means a host-id change can wipe visible cached rows.
2137	
2138	### Reconciler
2139	
2140	The relay state engine schedules:
2141	
2142	- boot reconciliation;
2143	- periodic reconciliation;
2144	- debounce reconciliation;
2145	- live lease expiry reconciliation;
2146	- forced reconciliation after some responses if state is empty, incomplete, or
2147	  stale.
2148	- archive mutation reconciliation, though the audited path has drift because
2149	  mutation ingestion can schedule generic Dock reconciliation rather than
2150	  guaranteed Archive reconciliation.
2151	
2152	Current constants include a periodic reconcile interval and short debounce.
2153	The important user-facing fact is simpler: Dock updates are not a direct push
2154	from every raw app-server event. They rely on relay reconciliation plus
2155	published deltas.
2156	
2157	Important relay constants from `scripts/dock-relay-constants.mjs`:
2158	
2159	| Constant | Current value | Why it matters |
2160	| --- | ---: | --- |
2161	| `RAW_APP_SERVER_PORT` | `4500` | Raw Codex app-server port. |
2162	| `DOCK_RELAY_PORT` | `4510` | Phone-facing relay port. |
2163	| `UPSTREAM_REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS` | `120_000` | Long upstream requests can wait up to 2 minutes. |
2164	| `UPSTREAM_RECONNECT_ATTEMPTS` | `2` | Detail upstream recovery attempts before downstream close. |
2165	| `UPSTREAM_RECONNECT_DELAY_MS` | `100` | Base delay between upstream reconnect attempts. |
2166	| `RELAY_STATE_RECONCILE_INTERVAL_MS` | `30_000` | Periodic Dock reconciliation cadence. |
2167	| `RELAY_STATE_RECONCILE_DEBOUNCE_MS` | `250` | Debounce for scheduled reconciliation. |
2168	| `RELAY_STATE_ARCHIVE_MUTATION_GRACE_MS` | `10_000` | Archive mutation bounce-back grace. |
2169	| `LIVE_STATUS_REFRESH_INTERVAL_MS` | `2_500` | Live status cache refresh cadence. |
2170	| `LIVE_STATUS_MAX_AGE_MS` | `5_000` | Live status cache age budget. |
2171	| `LIVE_LOADED_LIST_LIMIT` | `2_000` | Loaded-thread scan limit. |
2172	| `THREAD_LIST_MAX_LIMIT` | `250` | History page limit. |
2173	| `RELAY_STATE_DOCK_WINDOW_SIZE` | `500` | Stream snapshot/window row size. |
2174	| `RELAY_STATE_SNAPSHOT_SOFT_LIMIT_BYTES` | `1 MiB` | Snapshot soft cap before windowing. |
2175	| `RELAY_STATE_UPDATE_SOFT_LIMIT_BYTES` | `256 KiB` | Delta soft cap before snapshot fallback. |
2176	| `DEFAULT_MAX_OPEN_PER_LABEL` | `4` | Default upstream pool cap. |
2177	| `UPSTREAM_POOL_LIMITS.history` | `1` | History upstream pool cap. |
2178	| `UPSTREAM_POOL_LIMITS.live-status` | `4` | Live-status upstream pool cap. |
2179	
2180	### Live Status Cache And Session Router
2181	
2182	The relay tracks loaded/live rows and can route a thread to a live endpoint or
2183	history endpoint. Detail uses this to read live rows and list turns from the
2184	right upstream.
2185	
2186	Live disappearance has incomplete explicit publish bookkeeping. There is a
2187	`markLiveLeaseExpiryPublished` store method and live-disconnect stale-marking
2188	code. The audit found `NotificationIngestor.ingestLiveDisconnect` and
2189	`RelayStateStore.markLiveLeaseExpiryPublished`, but no production callers for
2190	either method. Practically, live disappearance
2191	relies on later reconciliation more than an explicit immediate stale publish.
2192	
2193	### Thread Summary Cache
2194	
2195	`scripts/dock-relay-thread-summary-cache.mjs` exists and
2196	`threadSummaryCacheForConfig` can construct it, but this audit did not find it
2197	on the Dock/Archive card-truth path in `dock-relay-state-engine.mjs`. It must
2198	not be treated as a separate ordering or freshness source unless future code
2199	wires it into the canonical projection and updates this contract.
2200	
2201	### Local Client Metadata
2202	
2203	Swift local metadata is fully specified in
2204	`Local Metadata And Host Identity`. It includes pins, labels, rails, and host
2205	alias migration only. It must not create production cards. A pinned row still
2206	needs a relay card underneath.
2207	
2208	### Saved Phone Config
2209	
2210	Saved phone config is intentionally small: it contains relay `hosts` only. Swift
2211	rejects saved `relayInstanceID` in phone-side config and rejects normal app
2212	endpoints on raw app-server port `4500`.
2213	
2214	Current nuance: saved relay config is cached inside the store actor, so an
2215	external rewrite of `relay-config.json` is not reread by that running app
2216	process.
2217	
2218	### Bootstrap And Bonjour
2219	
2220	Before any Dock data route runs, `RelayBootstrapStore` chooses a `HostRegistry`:
2221	
2222	1. Try `CODEX_DOCK_HOSTS` from the launch environment.
2223	2. If absent, start Bonjour discovery for `_codexdock._tcp.local.`.
2224	3. Load saved manual relay host config.
2225	4. Allow manual host/port entry.
2226	
2227	`BonjourRelayDiscovery` converts a discovered service into `DiscoveredRelay`
2228	with endpoint host/port, display name, and optional TXT `relay-id`. That
2229	bootstrap path selects relay endpoints only; it is not a card data source and
2230	does not prove Dock stream freshness.
2231	
2232	## Connectivity Model
2233	
2234	### AppServerClient Connection State
2235	
2236	Swift `AppServerClient` exposes connection states and can reconnect if its
2237	policy allows it.
2238	
2239	On transport loss:
2240	
2241	- pending requests fail;
2242	- transport disconnects;
2243	- if reconnect policy exists and initialization parameters exist, the client
2244	  starts reconnect;
2245	- reconnect reopens transport and repeats `initialize`;
2246	- streams are finished only when marked offline/error/closed.
2247	
2248	Important current mismatch: replaying `initialize` is not the same as replaying
2249	view subscriptions. A Dock stream subscription is stateful on the relay. If the
2250	client WebSocket reconnects but the `dock/subscribe` request is not replayed,
2251	the client can be connected but unsubscribed.
2252	
2253	Transport detail: `AppServerClient.markOffline` finishes notification and
2254	server-request streams, but the normal `.liveDetail` transport-loss reconnect
2255	path can reconnect and re-initialize without finishing the outer notification
2256	stream. That is why `DockStore` can miss the need to tear down and re-open the
2257	Dock stream.
2258	
2259	### Dock Connectivity
2260	
2261	Dock `DockStore` marks a stream failure when its update stream ends or throws.
2262	It retains rows, marks host partial/offline, closes the connection, and schedules
2263	a reconnect.
2264	
2265	If the underlying `AppServerClient` reconnects internally without ending the
2266	outer `updates()` stream, `DockStore` may not know it needs to reopen or
2267	resubscribe.
2268	
2269	### Client Connectivity UI Versus Stream Freshness
2270	
2271	The client has connectivity surfaces that can say a host is online or a route
2272	responded. That is not identical to card freshness.
2273	
2274	- `AppConnectivityStore` tracks host phases, route diagnostics, lifecycle
2275	  state, and detail live state.
2276	- `DockStore` and `ThreadCardTable` track card-stream freshness/completeness.
2277	- `ThreadDetailStore` tracks live detail state.
2278	- Relay `/routesz` and `/statusz` track route/process health.
2279	
2280	A healthy connectivity indicator can coexist with stale cards if the route
2281	responds but the stream is unsubscribed, the SQLite projection is old, or live
2282	endpoint proof failed. The UI must keep "can reach relay" separate from "this
2283	card/detail is current."
2284	
2285	### Host Connection Testing
2286	
2287	`CardStreamHostConnectionTester` is a one-shot probe:
2288	
2289	1. opens a new card stream connection;
2290	2. calls `dock/subscribe`;
2291	3. reads the returned snapshot row count;
2292	4. closes the connection.
2293	
2294	This is useful for Settings/host validation, but it is not evidence that the
2295	Dock Home long-lived stream is subscribed or fresh. It creates its own relay
2296	downstream session and its own temporary relay subscription, then removes that
2297	subscription on close.
2298	
2299	False confidence case:
2300	
2301	```text
2302	Dock Home stream silently reconnects without re-subscribing
2303	Settings host test opens a new connection
2304	Settings host test succeeds
2305	Dock Home stream remains unsubscribed
2306	User still sees old rows
2307	```
2308	
2309	Therefore host "Online" from a connection test means "a fresh one-shot
2310	`dock/subscribe` succeeded", not "the existing Dock UI stream is receiving
2311	updates."
2312	
2313	### Thread Detail Connectivity
2314	
2315	Thread Detail rehydrates when:
2316	
2317	- Swift sees a reconnecting -> connected transition while the detail is loaded
2318	  and `liveState == .reconnecting`;
2319	- app foreground resume happens and the session is connected;
2320	- stream end marks stale;
2321	- reconnect failure marks stale/error.
2322	
2323	Thread Detail does not periodically poll `thread/turns/list` while the WebSocket
2324	looks connected. It trusts the live session after resume.
2325	
2326	### Relay Upstream Recovery
2327	
2328	The relay can lose only the upstream app-server session and keep the phone
2329	WebSocket open. It then retries upstream `thread/resume`.
2330	
2331	That is dangerous for detail freshness:
2332	
2333	- Relay recovers upstream and resumes live notifications.
2334	- Phone WebSocket never closes.
2335	- Swift never observes reconnect.
2336	- Swift never re-runs `thread/read` plus `thread/turns/list`.
2337	- Notifications missed during the upstream outage may never appear until a
2338	  manual/foreground rehydrate.
2339	
2340	This is the cleanest explanation for a thread that appears open/connected but
2341	does not include current work.
2342	
2343	## Exception Scenarios
2344	
2345	### Empty Or Cold Relay Cache
2346	
2347	If SQLite has no rows, `dock/subscribe` may return empty or partial state, then
2348	the relay schedules reconciliation. Tests must distinguish "empty because no
2349	threads exist" from "empty because relay has not reconciled yet."
2350	
2351	If there is no sync scope, relay freshness can be `unknown`. If any sync scope
2352	is incomplete or any stored card proof is incomplete, freshness should be
2353	`stale`. Only fully proven scopes/cards should be `fresh`.
2354	
2355	### Stale SQLite Cache
2356	
2357	If SQLite contains old rows and the relay decides state is fresh enough,
2358	`dock/subscribe` can show old rows until periodic reconcile or a forced resync
2359	updates it.
2360	
2361	### Raw App-Server Down
2362	
2363	Relay process health can remain green while app-server route health or data
2364	freshness fails. Card streams should expose stale/partial freshness, not only
2365	connection success.
2366	
2367	### Route Healthy But Data Stale
2368	
2369	`/readyz` and route request counts do not prove Dock or detail data is fresh.
2370	A stale `dock/subscribe` response can still be a route success.
2371	
2372	### Sequence Gap
2373	
2374	Swift rejects a delta whose `baseSeq` does not match current sequence and calls
2375	`dock/resync`.
2376	
2377	### Schema Mismatch
2378	
2379	Swift rejects mismatched stream schema and calls `dock/resync`.
2380	
2381	### Epoch Change
2382	
2383	Swift treats epoch change as requiring resync.
2384	
2385	### Partial Window
2386	
2387	Swift can represent partial windows and mark host state partial until all rows
2388	are received.
2389	
2390	### Large Delta Snapshot Fallback
2391	
2392	Relay can send a snapshot instead of a delta when update payload is too large.
2393	Swift treats compatible snapshots as replacement state.
2394	
2395	### Subscribe-Time Race
2396	
2397	Relay protects the subscribe-time race by installing the subscriber before
2398	snapshot creation, buffering updates while the snapshot is produced, and sending
2399	only buffered updates whose sequence is newer than the snapshot. This is good
2400	stream design and should be preserved.
2401	
2402	This does not solve reconnect-without-resubscribe. A transparent client
2403	reconnect creates a new downstream socket/session at the relay, so the old
2404	subscription is removed and the new connection must subscribe again.
2405	
2406	### Malformed Update With Missing Params
2407	
2408	Current Swift stream client ignores a `dock/update` notification with missing
2409	params instead of treating it as stream corruption. That can hide a relay bug.
2410	
2411	### Compatible But Older Snapshot
2412	
2413	Current Swift table can accept a compatible snapshot without comparing whether
2414	it is older than current state. That can replace newer state if relay sends a
2415	stale snapshot fallback.
2416	
2417	### Non-Human Upsert For Existing Human Card
2418	
2419	Swift ignores non-human upserts. If a previously visible human card becomes
2420	non-human and relay sends only an upsert, the old visible row can remain. Relay
2421	must send an explicit delete for cards that leave the human card set.
2422	
2423	### Duplicate Card IDs
2424	
2425	Some Swift snapshot paths build dictionaries using unique keys. Duplicate card
2426	ids can crash or corrupt expectations if not rejected before dictionary
2427	construction.
2428	
2429	### Inconsistent Complete Window
2430	
2431	Window validation can allow `complete == true` with inconsistent totals. Tests
2432	should pin the intended contract.
2433	
2434	### Thread Detail Repeated Cursor
2435	
2436	Swift throws on repeated `thread/turns/list` cursor. Relay also treats repeated
2437	turn cursors as proof failure for card activity.
2438	
2439	### Thread Detail Resume Failure
2440	
2441	If initial history read succeeds but `thread/resume` fails, Swift keeps the
2442	historical detail and marks live state stale.
2443	
2444	### Thread Detail Notification Stream End
2445	
2446	If notification stream ends, Swift marks detail stale.
2447	
2448	### Thread Detail Server Request Stream End
2449	
2450	If server request stream ends, Swift marks detail stale.
2451	
2452	### Thread Closed
2453	
2454	Swift marks live state closed on `thread/closed`.
2455	
2456	### Missing Thread ID In Live Events
2457	
2458	Swift drops live notifications and requests whose params do not match the
2459	expected `threadId`. Relay forwards upstream requests and notifications as-is.
2460	If upstream omits `threadId`, the phone can drop a real event/request.
2461	
2462	### Server Request Resolution
2463	
2464	Swift can resolve request cards locally when the phone answers. It also has a
2465	path for upstream resolved notifications, but coverage is thin and missing
2466	`threadId` can prevent the normalizer from accepting the notification.
2467	
2468	### Multiple In-Progress Turns
2469	
2470	Swift currently picks the last in-progress turn from the normalized turn order.
2471	If app-server ever returns multiple active turns or descending order changes,
2472	the active turn selection can be wrong.
2473	
2474	### Background / Foreground
2475	
2476	Thread Detail marks live state stale on background and rehydrates on foreground
2477	resume. Dock refreshes on foreground via DockView. Dock stream reconnect itself
2478	is not gated the same way as Thread Detail's `AppServerClient` foreground gate.
2479	
2480	### Archive Mutation
2481	
2482	Archive/unarchive should update both Dock and Archive views. Current code can
2483	schedule Dock reconciliation without guaranteed Archive update.
2484	
2485	Archive mutation grace can suppress active re-adds for a short period after a
2486	local archive mark. If upstream archive state lags beyond that grace, a row can
2487	return to active on a later reconcile.
2488	
2489	### Archive Failure
2490	
2491	Archive stale writes can be mislabeled as Dock stale scope. Host freshness is
2492	global across scopes, so one view can stale another.
2493	
2494	### Live Attention Flags
2495	
2496	There is relay code for inspecting pending server requests and adding attention
2497	flags, but the audited Dock reconcile path does not call it. If this is still
2498	intended, it is currently drifted or dead.
2499	
2500	### Realtime Transcription
2501	
2502	Transcription state is relay-side and session-scoped. Phone-side provider
2503	config is rejected. Notifications must be observed independently of Dock and
2504	Thread Detail card streams.
2505	
2506	### Config Rewrite While App Is Running
2507	
2508	Swift caches saved relay config in the store actor. If a script rewrites the
2509	saved phone config while the app process is already running, that process may
2510	not reread the file until restarted or explicitly reloaded.
2511	
2512	## Bugs And Mismatches Found
2513	
2514	### 1. Dock WebSocket Reconnect Does Not Re-Subscribe
2515	
2516	Root cause: `AppServerClient` reconnect replays `initialize`, but
2517	`AppServerThreadCardStreamConnection` only calls `dock/subscribe` once during
2518	`DockStore.openStream`.
2519	
2520	Why this matters: after a transport reconnect, the socket can be connected but
2521	the relay has no active Dock subscription for that connection. The old rows
2522	remain on screen and no `dock/update` arrives.
2523	
2524	Evidence:
2525	
2526	- Stream client creates auto-reconnecting client:
2527	  `CodexDock/State/AppServerThreadCardStreamClient.swift:22`.
2528	- Dock subscribes once:
2529	  `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift:307`.
2530	- AppServerClient reconnect redoes initialize:
2531	  `CodexDock/AppServer/AppServerClient.swift:674`.
2532	- Stream connection listens for update notifications but has no reconnect
2533	  resubscribe hook:
2534	  `CodexDock/State/AppServerThreadCardStreamClient.swift:65`.
2535	
2536	### 2. Thread Detail Can Miss History After Relay Upstream Recovery
2537	
2538	Root cause: relay can recover upstream `thread/resume` while keeping the phone
2539	WebSocket open. Swift only rehydrates detail when it sees downstream reconnect,
2540	foreground resume, or stream end.
2541	
2542	Why this matters: any notifications missed during the upstream outage are not
2543	recovered by Swift because it never re-runs `thread/turns/list`.
2544	
2545	Evidence:
2546	
2547	- Relay upstream close handling:
2548	  `scripts/dock-relay.mjs:338`.
2549	- Relay upstream recovery retries `thread/resume`:
2550	  `scripts/dock-relay.mjs:360`.
2551	- Relay closes phone only after recovery failure:
2552	  `scripts/dock-relay.mjs:430`.
2553	- Swift rehydrate only runs from connection state/foreground paths:
2554	  `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:525` and
2555	  `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:642`.
2556	
2557	### 3. Route Health Does Not Measure Stream Freshness
2558	
2559	Root cause: route observability records request success, not the semantic
2560	freshness/completeness of card truth or the presence of passive updates.
2561	
2562	Why this matters: diagnostics can say the relay is healthy while the app shows
2563	day-old data.
2564	
2565	Evidence:
2566	
2567	- Diagnostics endpoints are defined in `scripts/dock-relay.mjs:696`.
2568	- `semanticRouteOutcome` is a simple success wrapper around handled requests.
2569	- Passive `dock/update` / `archive/update` are sent directly by state stream
2570	  code and are not route-health successes.
2571	- `/syncz` returns `state:"available"` without checking sync freshness.
2572	- Runtime relay-state health can be dropped by status code reading a different
2573	  runtime property name.
2574	
2575	### 4. Relay Contract Schema Is Looser Than Swift Runtime
2576	
2577	Root cause: JSON schema requires only the broad envelope fields, while Swift
2578	runtime rejects more stream states based on view, schema, epoch, sequence, and
2579	window semantics.
2580	
2581	Why this matters: contract checks can pass payloads that the app would reject
2582	and resync.
2583	
2584	Evidence:
2585	
2586	- Schema requires only `kind`, `schemaVersion`, `view`, `epoch`, and `seq`.
2587	- Swift table validation is in `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift:177`.
2588	
2589	### 5. Heartbeat Exists In Swift Contract But Not Relay Emission
2590	
2591	Root cause: Swift and schema know about `heartbeat`, but Node relay production
2592	emission appears snapshot/delta-only, and sync audit treats non-snapshot/delta
2593	as unknown.
2594	
2595	Why this matters: the intended freshness heartbeat behavior is not fully
2596	exercised end to end.
2597	
2598	### 6. Archive Update Path Has Drift
2599	
2600	Root cause: archive mutation ingestion schedules `StateReconciler.run`, and
2601	`StateReconciler.run` calls `RelayStateEngine.reconcileDock`. The mutation chain
2602	does not call `reconcileArchive`; `reconcileArchive` is currently scheduled only
2603	after `archive/subscribe` and `archive/resync`. Archive stale scope can also be
2604	recorded as Dock scope, and host freshness is global.
2605	
2606	Why this matters: Archive can fail to update or can stale Dock, and Dock can
2607	stale Archive.
2608	
2609	### 7. Live Endpoint Failure Can Be Hidden By History Completeness
2610	
2611	Root cause: live endpoint failures are counted during collection, but audited
2612	Dock reconcile code does not appear to use that failed endpoint count to mark
2613	the overall reconcile incomplete.
2614	
2615	Why this matters: current active Codex work can fail to affect Dock while
2616	history-derived card proof still looks complete.
2617	
2618	### 8. Thread Detail Event Coverage Is Partial
2619	
2620	Root cause: Swift normalizes a selected set of live notification methods.
2621	Older app-server docs list more event types than the current client handles.
2622	
2623	Why this matters: live detail can look incomplete if unhandled events are
2624	important and do not later appear in historical turns.
2625	
2626	### 9. `thread/turns/list` Does Not Request `itemsView`
2627	
2628	Root cause: Swift sends thread id, cursor, limit, and sort direction, but not
2629	`itemsView`. Older docs suggest the app-server default may be summary.
2630	
2631	Why this matters: after reload/rehydrate, command/tool/file/compaction detail
2632	may be missing if the default view omits it.
2633	
2634	Canonical fix direction: make full item view part of the phone/relay contract.
2635	The intended target shape is `itemsView:"full"` on every Thread Detail
2636	`thread/turns/list` request. Swift should encode it or relay should inject it
2637	for phone detail routes, and tests should assert the actual outbound params.
2638	
2639	### 10. Missing `dock/update` Params Are Silently Ignored
2640	
2641	Root cause: stream client continues when notification params are absent.
2642	
2643	Why this matters: malformed relay updates can leave stale rows without forcing
2644	resync or surfacing a stream error.
2645	
2646	### 11. Compatible Older Snapshot Can Replace Newer State
2647	
2648	Root cause: Swift applies compatible snapshots as replacement state without
2649	checking if they are older than current host state.
2650	
2651	Why this matters: a stale snapshot fallback or replay can move the UI backward.
2652	
2653	## What The Current Tests Prove
2654	
2655	### Debug Scripted Bypass
2656	
2657	In `#if DEBUG`, `CodexDockBootstrapView` can replace real relay-backed
2658	implementations when `CODEX_DOCK_UI_DOCK_STREAM_SCENARIO` is set:

`UpstreamConnectionPool` reuses healthy upstream clients by `(label, url,
bearerToken hash)` and replaces unhealthy clients. It limits open connections
per label.

Current constants:

- history pool limit: `1`;
- live-status pool limit: `4`;
- default max open per label: `4`;
- upstream request timeout: `120_000 ms`;
- upstream reconnect attempts for live detail: `2`;
- upstream reconnect base delay: `100 ms`;
- upstream reconnect jitter: `25 ms`.

This is why "relay connected" is not one thing. The relay may have:

- a healthy downstream phone socket;
- an unhealthy history upstream pool client;
- a stale live-status cache;
- a recovered dedicated detail upstream;
- a healthy `/readyz` process endpoint.

Those states need separate diagnostics.

### Poll/Reconcile, Not Raw Push

Dock card updates are not raw app-server push subscriptions. The relay builds
card truth through reconciliation:

1. poll live loaded rows;
2. poll history `thread/list`;
3. validate/enrich rows with `thread/read`;
4. supplement from `session_index.jsonl`;
5. prove newest activity with `thread/turns/list`;
6. write SQLite;
7. publish `dock/update`.

Thread Detail live events are different: after `thread/resume`, the relay
forwards raw upstream notifications and server requests from that dedicated
upstream session.

### Reconcile And Canonicalization Algorithm

The relay card pipeline is not a flat `thread/list` passthrough. The canonical
collapse points are `aggregateThreadList`, `canonicalizeThreadRows`,
`normalizeThread`, and `RelayStateStore.applyDockReconciliation` /
`applyArchiveReconciliation`.

History list drain:

1. `drainThreadListRows` starts with human-only params by removing
   `sourceKind` / `sourceKinds` and clamping `limit` to
   `THREAD_LIST_MAX_LIMIT`.
2. It calls history `thread/list`.
3. It appends every row with `ordinal`, `pageIndex`, and `rowIndex`.
4. It follows `nextCursor`.
5. Repeated cursors mark the scope incomplete with an error.
6. Thrown upstream errors mark the scope incomplete with an error.

Human-started enrichment:

1. `enrichHumanStartedRows` runs `classifyThreadOrigin` on list rows.
2. Rejected rows increment `rejectedCounts`.
3. Accepted candidates are read again through `thread/read includeTurns:false`.
4. `mergeAuthoritativeThreadRead` overlays read metadata onto list metadata.
5. It preserves list `id`.
6. It preserves the newest `createdAt`/`updatedAt` between list and read so
   read metadata cannot downgrade the activity baseline.
7. It deletes embedded `turns`.
8. The merged row is classified again; failures are rejected.

Session-index supplement:

1. Relay reads `CODEX_HOME/session_index.jsonl`.
2. It keeps latest row per thread id not already present.
3. It sorts by `updatedAtMs` descending.
4. It validates each candidate with `thread/read`.
5. It rejects candidates that do not match active/archive scope.
6. It merges supplement rows after existing rows.
7. It sorts the merged set by `updatedAt` descending with original insertion
   order as tie-breaker.

Live overlay:

1. `collectLiveRows` asks each configured live endpoint for
   `thread/loaded/list`.
2. For each loaded thread id, relay calls `thread/read includeTurns:false`.
3. Non-human rows are rejected.
4. Duplicate live rows are collapsed by `preferThread`.
5. `preferThread` chooses lower status priority first:
   waiting-on-approval/input, running, idle, error, unknown, not loaded.
6. Ties choose the row with newer `updatedAt` / `createdAt`.
7. `orderedDockRows` overlays live status onto matching stored/history rows.

Activity proof:

1. `canonicalizeThreadRows` is the required card-truth proof step.
2. For each accepted row, relay computes `baseActivityAtMs` from:
   `activityAtMs`, `activityAt`, `updatedAtMs`, `updatedAt`, `createdAtMs`,
   `createdAt`.
3. Relay drains all `thread/turns/list` pages for that thread.
   Current relay proof calls do not pass `itemsView`. That is acceptable only
   for Dock card ordering because the relay needs turn timestamps, not full
   item bodies. It must not be reused as proof that Thread Detail has full item
   content.
4. For each turn, relay considers `activityAtMs`, `activityAt`,
   `updatedAtMs`, `updatedAt`, `completedAtMs`, `completedAt`,
   `finishedAtMs`, `finishedAt`, `startedAtMs`, `startedAt`,
   `createdAtMs`, `createdAt`, `timestampMs`, and `timestamp`.
5. The canonical `activityAtMs` is the max of thread activity and newest turn
   activity.
6. `activityAt` is the ISO string for canonical activity.
7. `orderKey` is `activityOrderKey(activityAtMs, threadID)`.
8. Success emits `freshness:"fresh"`, `completeness:"complete"`,
   `activityProofStatus:"proven"`,
   `activityProofSource:"thread/read+thread/turns/list"`.
9. If turn proof fails, the fallback row uses thread activity only and emits
   `freshness:"stale"`, `completeness:"partial"`,
   `activityProofStatus:"unproven"`,
   `activityProofSource:"thread/read+thread/turns/list:error"`.
10. Any proof failure makes the reconcile scope incomplete.

Ordering key:

```text
activityOrderKey = pad(Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER - activityAtMs, 16) + ":" + threadID
```

This makes lexicographic ascending SQLite order equivalent to newest activity
first. Swift may use `orderKey` as relay-owned order truth; it must not invent
new recency from message text, list index, or local pin state.

Normalization:

`normalizeThread` converts a canonical row into `DockThreadCardDTO` facts:

- `id`: `<logicalHostID>::<threadID>`;
- `backendSessionID`: `sessionId` or `threadID`;
- `status`: `active` flags map to `needsApproval`, `needsInput`, or
  `running`; raw `idle` maps to `idle`; `systemError` maps to `error`;
  `notLoaded` maps to `dormant`;
- `lane`: human sources (`cli`, `vscode`, `atlas`, `chatgpt`) map to `human`,
  otherwise fallback lane;
- `sourceKind`: `human` for human lane, `automation` for agent lane;
- `archiveState`: active or archived depending on the reconcile path;
- `repository`, `workingDirectory`, `branch`, `displaySummary`, `title`, and
  `summarySource` are bounded display facets.

SQLite write and delete semantics:

- `applyDockReconciliation` writes active cards, marks `active_scope_present`,
  and marks missing previous active rows inactive only when the scope is
  complete.
- Fresh local archive mutations suppress active re-adds for
  `RELAY_STATE_ARCHIVE_MUTATION_GRACE_MS`.
- `applyArchiveReconciliation` writes archived cards, marks
  `archived_scope_present`, and marks missing previous archive rows not archived
  only when the archive scope is complete.
- Both paths call `recordSyncScope`.
- Both paths write a row into `changes` and return `{ seq, upsertCards,
  deleteCardIDs }`.
- Subscribers publish deltas from those returned upserts/deletes.

### Relay-Side Detail Routing

The client calls `thread/read` and `thread/turns/list` on the relay, but the
relay decides where those calls go.

- `aggregateThreadRead`:
  - requires `threadId`;
  - checks `SessionRouter.rowForThread`;
  - if live and `includeTurns:false`, returns the sanitized live row;
  - if live and `includeTurns:true`, reads that thread from the live endpoint;
  - otherwise reads history;
  - always verifies the thread is human-started.
- `listThreadTurns`:
  - requires `threadId`;
  - verifies the thread is human-started;
  - chooses live endpoint or history endpoint;
  - forwards `thread/turns/list` with the client params.

This matters for compaction and freshness: Swift thinks it is draining one
logical thread history, while the relay may route that drain to history or to a
live endpoint depending on current loaded status.

## Card DTO And Contract Fields

The generated Swift DTOs come from
`contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json` through
`scripts/generate-dock-thread-card-contract.mjs`.

Important stream fields:

- `kind`: `snapshot`, `delta`, or `heartbeat`.
- `schemaVersion`: expected stream schema version.
- `view`: `dock` or `archive`.
- `epoch`: relay subscription generation.
- `baseSeq`: sequence the delta expects the client to currently have.
- `seq`: relay state sequence after the update.
- `stateGeneration`: relay state generation value.
- `complete`: whether the delivered view/window is complete.
- `totalRows`: total row count for the view.
- `window`: offset, limit, row count, optional next offset.
- `freshness`: stream-level status plus attempt/sync/error metadata.
- `hosts`: full host rows in snapshots.
- `cards`: full card rows in snapshots.
- `upsertHosts`, `upsertCards`, `deleteCardIDs`: delta payload.

Important card fields:

- `id`: stable card id, normally host/thread composite.
- `logicalHostID`: relay logical host identity.
- `threadID`: raw Codex thread id.
- `backendSessionID`: app-server/backend session id.
- `hostDisplayName` and `hostEndpoint`: display/debug host facts.
- `orderKey`: relay-owned sort key. Swift must render by this, not invent
  recency.
- `activityAt` and `activityAtMs`: proven activity time, folded from thread
  metadata and newest turn activity.
- `displaySummary`, `title`, `summarySource`: user-facing summary facts.
- `status`: running, needs input, needs approval, idle, error, dormant,
  unknown.
- `sourceKind`: human, automation, unknown.
- `lane`: human, agent, unknown.
- `relationship` and `forkedFromID`: root/forked/spawned lineage.
- `archiveState`: active, archived, unknown.
- `freshness`: per-card freshness status.
- `completeness`: per-card completeness status.
- `repository`, `workingDirectory`, `branch`: project facets.

The contract drift risk is that JSON schema can validate broad shape while
Swift runtime enforces stricter stream semantics. A payload can be schema-valid
but still require Swift resync.

Every production and fixture consumer of `ThreadCardStreamConnecting` must be

## Local Metadata And Host Identity

Phone-local metadata and host aliasing are allowed only as decoration and
identity resolution. They must never create rows, change recency, or override
relay card truth.

### Local Metadata Contract

Persistence owner:

- file store: `FileLocalThreadMetadataStore`;
- default path: user Application Support `CodexDock/thread-metadata.json`;
- logical entries are encoded as `{ key, metadata }` pairs;
- key shape: `{ hostID, backendSessionID, threadID }`.

Allowed local metadata fields:

| Field | Meaning | Can affect card truth? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `label` | Local user label, trimmed; empty becomes nil. | No. |
| `rail` | Local color rail. | No. |
| `isPinned` | Local pin flag. | Ordering within pinned UI group only. |
| `pinnedAt` | Local pin timestamp; nil when unpinned. | No relay recency effect. |
| `pinnedOrder` | Local pinned-row order. | Pinned UI order only. |

Forbidden local metadata fields:

- `title`
- `status`
- `activityAt`
- `activityAtMs`
- `orderKey`
- `displaySummary`
- `freshness`
- `completeness`
- `archiveState`
- `repository`
- `workingDirectory`
- `branch`
- any field that could create, delete, archive, unarchive, freshen, stale, or
  reorder a relay card outside the explicit pinned-row UI.

Merge/decorate layer:

- `ThreadCardRowProjector` creates rows only from delivered
  `DockThreadCardDTO` values.
- It looks up metadata by exact `{ logicalHostID, backendSessionID, threadID }`.
- If exact lookup misses, it may use `DockHostIdentityResolver` to map an old
  metadata host alias to the current logical host id.
- It applies only `rail`, `label`, `isPinned`, `pinnedAt`, and `pinnedOrder`.
- It always takes title, status, activity, `orderKey`, summary, freshness,
  archive state, repository, working directory, and branch from the relay card.

Migration:

- `LocalMetadataEngine.migrateHostAliases` rewrites metadata keys to the
  observed relay logical host id only when `DockHostIdentityResolver` has an
  observed logical identity for that alias.
- When multiple old keys collapse to one logical key, metadata merge rules are:
  - keep existing label unless missing;
  - keep existing rail unless missing;
  - pin if either side is pinned;
  - keep earliest `pinnedAt`;
  - keep lowest `pinnedOrder`;
  - normalize pinned order after merge.

No production code may use local metadata as a card source. If a relay card is
absent, local metadata must not render a row.

### Host Identity Resolution Contract

Three host ids can appear in the client:

| Name | Source | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Configured host id | `DockHostConfiguration.id` | The saved/launch endpoint entry Swift is using. |
| Stream host id | `DockStreamHostDTO.id` | Host id emitted by the relay stream. |
| Logical host id | `DockStreamHostDTO.logicalHostID` and `DockThreadCardDTO.logicalHostID` | Relay-owned stable host identity used in `HostScopedThreadID`. |

`DockHostIdentityResolver` owns client-side alias resolution:

1. Group observations by configured host id.
2. For each configured host, choose the first observed logical host id from
   stream hosts/cards; otherwise fall back to configured host id.
3. Build aliases from:
   - configured host id;
   - configured display name;
   - configured endpoint display string;
   - observed stream host id;
   - observed logical host id;
   - observed display name;
   - observed endpoint.
4. Store exact aliases and lowercased normalized aliases.
5. `logicalHostID(forAlias:sourceConfiguredHostID:)` returns:
   - the source configured host's logical id when the source host is known and
     the alias is empty/compatible with that source;
   - a logical id only when the alias maps to exactly one logical host;
   - nil for ambiguous aliases.
6. `resolve(rowHostID:sourceConfiguredHostID:preferredConfiguredHostID:)`
   chooses a configured host record in this order:
   - source configured host id;
   - preferred configured host id;
   - a loaded/partial/empty host status;
   - first record in registry order.
7. `contains(rowHostID:sourceConfiguredHostID:in:)` requires the row alias to
   resolve to the expected logical host id for that configured host.

Why this matters:

- Multi-endpoint setups can have multiple configured host entries that point at
  the same relay logical host.
- Rows use relay logical host ids, while settings/actions often need the
  configured endpoint used to make the request.
- A wrong alias match can make the UI look connected to one host while row
  actions go to another configured endpoint.

Hard rule: host aliasing can choose which configured endpoint owns an already
delivered relay row. It must not create a row, merge rows from two logical
hosts, or use endpoint aliases as card truth.

## Dock Home End-To-End Flow

1. Swift creates an `AppServerThreadCardStreamClient`.
2. The stream client creates `AppServerClient(webSocketURL: relay, bearerToken:
   nil, connectionPolicy: .liveDetail)`.
3. Swift connects and sends `initialize`/`initialized`.
4. `DockStore.openStream` calls `dock/subscribe`.
5. Relay returns a snapshot from SQLite state.
6. Relay's subscription code installs the subscriber before reading the
   snapshot, buffers updates that arrive during snapshot creation, then sends
   only buffered updates newer than the returned snapshot.
7. Swift `ThreadCardTable.applySnapshot` validates schema, view, window, and
   host/card policy.
8. `DockStore.startUpdateTask` starts reading `dock/update`.
9. Relay periodically reconciles app-server state:
   - reads live rows from loaded sessions;
   - reads history with `thread/list`;
   - validates human-started rows with `thread/read`;
   - adds session-index supplements;
   - proves activity through `thread/turns/list`;
   - writes card facts to SQLite;
   - publishes `dock/update`.
10. Swift `ThreadCardTable.applyUpdate` applies deltas if `baseSeq` matches,
   otherwise requests `dock/resync`.
11. `DockRenderProjector` converts accepted cards plus local metadata into
    visible rows.
12. `DockCardProjection` filters/searches/groups rows, but recency remains
    relay-owned.
