Confirmed: `orderKey: String` and `activityAtMs: Int64` are both non-optional relay-provided fields. Now I have complete evidence for all 8 claims. Let me compile the findings.

## Audit Findings: SWIFT Dock Card Stream + Reconnect Handling

All anchors verified against actual code. CWD: `/Users/aelaguiz/workspace/codex-client`.

---

### 1. SUBSCRIBE ONCE — CONFIRMED

`dock/subscribe` is sent exactly once per `openStream`, via `connection.subscribe()`. It is NOT wired into the transport-reconnect path.

`CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift:295-321` (`openStream`):
```swift
let connection = try await streamClient.connect(to: host)   // :304 — connect + initialize
openedConnection = connection
streamConnections[host.id] = connection
let snapshot = try await connection.subscribe()             // :307 — the ONLY dock/subscribe call site
try await applySubscribedSnapshot(snapshot, host: host, connection: connection)
startUpdateTask(host: host, connection: connection)         // :309
```

`subscribe()` itself sends `dock/subscribe` as a one-shot request — `AppServerThreadCardStreamClient.swift:95-111`, route resolved at `:138-145` (`AppServerMethods.dockSubscribe`). The subscribe call lives in `DockStore`/`AppServerThreadCardStreamConnection`, entirely above the `AppServerClient` transport layer. `AppServerClient`'s reconnect loop (next section) has no reference to `subscribe`/`dockSubscribe`. So a transparent transport reconnect inside `AppServerClient` does NOT re-invoke `dock/subscribe`. Confirmed, and this matches the doc's stated failure mode (reference doc lines 30-32, 41-42).

---

### 2. RECONNECT REPLAYS INITIALIZE ONLY — CONFIRMED

Policy `.liveDetail` carries a reconnect policy: `AppServerClient.swift:33-41`. The stream client constructs its `AppServerClient` with `.liveDetail` at `AppServerThreadCardStreamClient.swift:23`.

Reconnect routine `runReconnectLoop` — `AppServerClient.swift:674-723`:
```swift
guard let reconnect = connectionPolicy.reconnect,
      let params = initializeParams else { ... }            // :675-676 — replays stored initializeParams only
...
try await openTransport(mode: .reconnecting)               // :707 — reopen transport
_ = try await completeInitializeHandshake(params: params, timeout: initializeTimeout)  // :708 — initialize + initialized only
reconnectTask = nil
```

`completeInitializeHandshake` (`:480-489`) sends only `initialize` + the `initialized` notification, then `setState(.connected)`. There is NO `dock/subscribe` replay anywhere in the reconnect path — `AppServerClient` has no knowledge of dock methods.

Crucially, on transport loss the reconnect path does NOT finish the outer notification stream. `handleTransportLoss` (`:647-661`):
```swift
failAllPending(with: .disconnected(reason))   // :650 — fails in-flight requests
await transport.disconnect()                  // :651
guard connectionPolicy.reconnect != nil, initializeParams != nil, !isExplicitlyDisconnected else {
    markOffline(reason)                       // :656 — ONLY here is the stream finished
    return
}
startReconnect(reason: reason)                // :660 — notificationContinuation NOT finished
```

`markOffline` (`:838-844`) is the only path in transport-loss handling that finishes the notification stream:
```swift
private func markOffline(_ reason: String) {
    failAllPending(with: .disconnected(reason))
    setState(.offline(reason: reason))
    notificationContinuation.finish()         // :842
    serverRequestContinuation.finish()        // :843
}
```

So with `.liveDetail`, on a transient drop the client goes `reconnecting`, the notification `updates()` stream stays open, transport+`initialize` are replayed, but the relay-side `dock/subscribe` subscription is gone. `markOffline` (which would finish the stream and let `DockStore` notice) is only reached when reconnect is disabled, `initializeParams` is nil, the client was explicitly disconnected, or reconnect attempts are EXHAUSTED (`runReconnectLoop` :722). **This confirms the central live-update bug: a `.liveDetail` reconnect can silently leave the Dock stream unsubscribed with no stream-end signal.**

---

### 3. STREAM-END DETECTION — CONFIRMED (with a caveat)

`startUpdateTask` — `DockStore.swift:342-362`:
```swift
streamTasks[host.id] = Task { [weak self, host, connection] in
    do {
        for try await update in connection.updates() {            // :346
            await self?.handleStreamUpdate(update, host: host, connection: connection)
        }
        if !Task.isCancelled {                                    // :349 — stream ended without throwing
            await self?.handleStreamFailure(
                DockRequestFailure.offline("Relay stream closed"), // :351
                host: host, connection: connection)
        }
    } catch is CancellationError {
        return
    } catch {
        await self?.handleStreamFailure(error, host: host, connection: connection)  // :359 — stream threw
    }
}
```

Failure handler `handleStreamFailure` — `DockStore.swift:425-441`: drops the connection/task (`:431-432`), closes the connection (`:433`), marks failure (`:434`, retains rows as partial/offline), publishes (`:435`), logs row retention (`:437-439`), then `scheduleReconnect` (`:440`).

`scheduleReconnect` (`:443-455`) sleeps `streamReconnectDelay` then calls `openStream` again (`:453`) — which DOES re-subscribe (`subscribe()` at :307). So when the stream actually ends, recovery is correct and re-subscribes.

The caveat that ties back to #2: this only fires when `connection.updates()` ends or throws. The `updates()` stream (`AppServerThreadCardStreamConnection.swift:66-87`) ends only when `client.notifications` ends — which, per #2, does NOT happen on a `.liveDetail` transient reconnect. So `handleStreamFailure`/`scheduleReconnect` are never triggered for the silent-unsubscribe case. Rows are retained on detected failures (`markFailure` → `.partial`, `ThreadCardTable.swift:67-80`).

---

### 4. RESYNC TRIGGERS — CONFIRMED, four reasons

Enum: `ThreadCardTable.swift:3-8` — `schemaMismatch`, `streamContract`, `epochMismatch`, `sequenceGap`.

Validations:

- **Schema mismatch** — `applySnapshot` :83-85 and `applyUpdate` :120-122 call `acceptsSchemaVersion` (:170-175): nil or `!= CodexDockConstants.Dock.streamSchemaVersion` → `.needsResync(.schemaMismatch)`.
- **Stream contract / view mismatch / window contract** — `acceptsStreamContract` (:177-209). View: `guard update.view == .dock else { return false }` (:178). Snapshot must carry `complete`/`totalRows`/`window` (:183-185) and pass `acceptsWindowContract`. Window contract `acceptsWindowContract` (:211-229): requires non-negative `totalRows`/offset/limit/rowCount, `window.rowCount == cardCount` (:221), rejects `nextOffset <= offset` (:224-225), and requires `complete || rowCount <= totalRows` (:228). Failure → `.needsResync(.streamContract)`.
- **Epoch change** — `applyUpdate` :127-130: `guard var state = statesByHostID[host.id], state.epoch == update.epoch else { return .needsResync(.epochMismatch) }`.
- **Sequence gap (baseSeq mismatch)** — `applyUpdate` :132-140: heartbeat requires `state.seq == update.seq` (:134); delta requires `update.baseSeq == state.seq` (:138), else `.needsResync(.sequenceGap)`.

`DockStore.handleStreamUpdate` :374-376 turns `.needsResync` into a `connection.resync()` (`dock/resync`) over the same connection.

---

### 5. SILENT-IGNORE EDGE CASES

**(a) `dock/update` with MISSING params is silently ignored — CONFIRMED.**
`AppServerThreadCardStreamClient.swift:76-80`:
```swift
guard let params = notification.params else {
    continue   // :78 — missing params skipped, NOT treated as corruption/finish
}
updateContinuation.yield(try params.decoded(as: ThreadCardStreamUpdateDTO.self))
```
Note the asymmetry: a missing-params notification is silently skipped (`continue`), but a present-but-undecodable params finishes the stream with an error (`:81-84`). So a malformed/empty `dock/update` does not advance state and does not trigger resync or reconnect.

**(b) A compatible-but-OLDER snapshot can replace newer state with no recency check — CONFIRMED.**
`ThreadCardTable.applySnapshot` :82-113 validates only schema (:83) and stream-contract/window (:86), then unconditionally overwrites `epoch`, `seq`, `cards`, etc. (:90-111). It never compares incoming `update.seq` or `update.stateGeneration` against the existing `state.seq`/generation. The DTO even carries `stateGeneration: Int64?` (`DockThreadCardDTO.swift:444`) and `seq` (:447), but `HostStreamState` stores no generation and `applySnapshot` reads neither for recency. A stale snapshot (from a delayed `dock/subscribe`/`dock/resync` response) silently clobbers newer applied state. Delta/heartbeat paths DO guard seq (:134/:138), but snapshot does not.

**(c) Non-human upsert for an existing human card is ignored, so a stale human row can remain if relay only upserts and never deletes — CONFIRMED.**
`ThreadCardTable.applyUpdate` delta branch :145-147:
```swift
for card in (update.upsertCards ?? []).filter(\.isAppFacingHumanThreadCard) {
    state.cardsByID[card.id] = card
}
```
`isAppFacingHumanThreadCard` = `lane == .human && sourceKind == .human` (`HumanThreadCardPolicy.swift:4-6`). If a card transitions human→non-human and the relay sends it as an upsert (not in `deleteCardIDs`), the filter drops it from the upsert loop, so the previously stored human entry in `cardsByID` is never overwritten or removed — the stale human row persists. Removal happens only via explicit `deleteCardIDs` (:148-150). Same human filter also gates the snapshot path (:99-104) and the render projector (`ThreadCardRowProjector.swift:10`, `DockRenderProjector` rows).

**(d) Duplicate card ids could crash dictionary construction — CONFIRMED (snapshot path only).**
`ThreadCardTable.applySnapshot` :98-104:
```swift
state.cardsByID = Dictionary(
    uniqueKeysWithValues: (update.cards ?? [])
        .filter(\.isAppFacingHumanThreadCard)
        .map { card in (card.id, card) }
)
```
`Dictionary(uniqueKeysWithValues:)` traps at runtime on duplicate keys. If a snapshot (`dock/subscribe`/`dock/resync` response or `kind:"snapshot"` update) contains two cards with the same `id`, this is a fatal crash. (The delta path at :146 uses subscripted assignment, which is dedup-safe; only the snapshot path is exposed.) The same crashing pattern exists in `ThreadCardTable.reset` :43-47 over host ids, and benign uniqueness assumptions in `DockRenderProjector` / `DockCardProjection` (`hostGroups` :91 keys by host id, safe).

---

### 6. ORDER-KEY OWNERSHIP — CONFIRMED

Swift renders the relay's `orderKey` and never rebuilds recency from timestamps/text/pin for the body sort.

DTO: `DockThreadCardDTO.swift:349 public let orderKey: String` (non-optional, relay-provided). `activityAtMs: Int64` (:351) is also relay-provided and required; `ThreadCardRowProjector.activityDate` (:75-79) only derives a display string, with the comment "The relay owns card recency."

Sort sites:
- `ThreadCardTable.sortedCards` :285-296 — `lhs.orderKey < rhs.orderKey`, id tiebreak.
- `DockCardProjection.rowPrecedesByRelayOrder` :358-379 — comment "The relay owns card ordering. Swift may filter and group rows, but it must not rebuild recency from timestamps or local status," compares `orderKey`, falls back to title then `hostID::threadID` (no timestamp).
- Group ordering `groupPrecedes` :338-356 — orders by `orderKey` (group orderKey = `rows.first?.orderKey`, :114/:138).

The only timestamp/pin-based sort is `pinnedRowPrecedes` (:381-401), which orders pinned rows by local `pinnedOrder`/`pinnedAt` — that is local pin ordering, separate from card recency, and consistent with the contract (reference doc rule 5, line 86-87).

---

### 7. CONNECTION TEST vs STREAM FRESHNESS — CONFIRMED

`CardStreamHostConnectionTester.testConnection` — `HostConnectionTesting.swift:22-35`:
```swift
connection = try await streamClient.connect(to: host)   // :25 — fresh connect+initialize
let snapshot = try await connection?.subscribe()        // :26 — one-shot dock/subscribe
await connection?.close()                                // :27 — immediately closed
return HostConnectionTestResult(
    rowCount: snapshot?.totalRows ?? snapshot?.cards?.count ?? 0)
```

It builds its own `AppServerThreadCardStreamClient` (default arg, :18), connects, subscribes once, and `close()`s right away. `close()` (`AppServerThreadCardStreamClient.swift:132-136`) cancels the notification task and calls `client.disconnect()`. This is an ephemeral connection entirely separate from `DockStore.streamConnections`; it never touches the long-lived Dock Home stream and is not evidence that stream is still subscribed. Matches reference doc line 728.

---

### 8. FOREGROUND/REFRESH — CONFIRMED

`refresh()` → `reload(showLoading: false)` — `DockStore.swift:166-168`. `reload` calls `synchronizeStreams()` at `:269`.

`synchronizeStreams` — `DockStore.swift:277-293`:
```swift
for host in hosts {
    if let connection = streamConnections[host.id] {
        await resync(host: host, connection: connection)   // :288 — EXISTING connection → dock/resync
    } else {
        await openStream(host: host)                       // :290 — only when no connection exists
    }
}
```

`resync` (:323-340) calls `connection.resync()` → `dock/resync` (`AppServerThreadCardStreamClient.swift:113-126`, route :156-163) over the **existing** connection. It does NOT call `subscribe()` and does NOT tear down/reopen the socket when a connection object already exists.

Therefore, in the silent-unsubscribe scenario from #2 (the `AppServerClient` transparently reconnected, so `streamConnections[host.id]` still holds a live-looking connection but the relay subscription is gone), `refresh()`/foreground takes the `resync` branch and sends `dock/resync` down a socket the relay no longer treats as a Dock subscriber. **`refresh()` cannot re-establish a lost subscription** — it only re-subscribes via `openStream` when the connection object is entirely absent (which only happens after `handleStreamFailure` clears it, which itself never fires in the silent case). The only `repeat` is the pagination loop (line 586); no timer/poll exists. The two rehydrate triggers are exactly: connection-state `.connected` -> `startRehydrateAfterReconnectIfNeeded` (line 532) and foreground resume while connected (line 517). I have all evidence. Here are my structured findings.

---

# Swift Thread Detail Live-Update Architecture Audit

All anchors verified against current working-tree source. The reference doc `docs/CODEX_DOCK_PROTOCOL_AND_UPDATE_ARCHITECTURE_REFERENCE_2026-05-31.md` is accurate; specific line-number cross-checks and the one minor staleness flag are noted at the end.

## 1. LOAD ORDER — CONFIRMED (exact match to claim)

The orchestration is in `ThreadDetailStore.load()`:

- `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift:261` — `let fullRead = try await readFullThread(session: session)`
- `:263` — `try await replaceEvents(from: fullRead.thread, liveState: .connecting)`
- `:266-269` — `let liveThread = try await resumeCompactThread(session: session, turns: fullRead.turns)`
- `:270` — `try await replaceEvents(from: liveThread, liveState: .live)`
- `:271` — `await replayBufferedInitialLiveEvents()`

Note buffering starts before any reads so live events arriving during load are not lost: `:258` `beginBufferingInitialLiveEvents()` then `:259` `startObservation(session: session)`.

**`readFullThread`** (`:563-579`) does read-then-drain:
```swift
let readResponse = try await session.threadRead(
    params: ThreadReadParams(threadId: row.id.threadID, includeTurns: false), ...)   // :569-571
let turns = try await readAllTurns(session: session)                                 // :573
return FullThreadRead(thread: readResponse.thread.replacingTurns(turns), turns: turns) // :575-578
```

**Pagination loop** `readAllTurns` (`:581-609`) — desc, paged until `nextCursor` nil/empty, with repeated-cursor guard:
```swift
params: ThreadTurnsListParams(threadId: row.id.threadID, cursor: cursor,
                              limit: Self.turnPageLimit, sortDirection: .desc)  // :588-593
turns.append(contentsOf: response.data)                                         // :596
guard let nextCursor = response.nextCursor, !nextCursor.isEmpty else { cursor = nil; break }  // :598-601
guard seenCursors.insert(nextCursor).inserted else {
    throw ThreadDetailStoreError.repeatedTurnsCursor(nextCursor) }              // :602-604
```
`turnPageLimit = 250` (`CodexDock/Configuration/CodexDockConstants.swift:21`).

**Resume + merge** `resumeCompactThread` (`:611-626`) requests `excludeTurns:true` then overwrites the compact resume turns with the drained turns:
```swift
let resumeResponse = try await session.threadResume(
    params: ThreadResumeParams(threadId: row.id.threadID, excludeTurns: true), ...)  // :620-623
return resumeResponse.thread.replacingTurns(turns)                                    // :625
```
The replacement (`replacingTurns(turns)` with the previously drained `fullRead.turns`) is the "replace compact resume turns with drained turns" step. Claim fully confirmed.

## 2. REHYDRATE TRIGGERS — CONFIRMED (exactly two; no periodic poll)

A "rehydrate" = `rehydrateAfterReconnect()` (`:642-667`), which re-runs `readFullThread` (`:656`) + `resumeCompactThread` (`:657`) then `mergeEvents` (`:658`). It fires from exactly two sites:

1. **Downstream reconnect transition while `liveState == .reconnecting`** — `handle(connectionState:)` `.connected` case calls `startRehydrateAfterReconnectIfNeeded()` (`:531-532`). That guard (`:628-640`) requires `case let .reconnecting(reason) = liveState` and `recoveryTask == nil`:
```swift
guard !isClosing, recoveryTask == nil, case .loaded = state,
      case let .reconnecting(reason) = liveState, let session else { return }  // :629-634
```
   `liveState` only becomes `.reconnecting` via `markLiveSessionReconnecting` (`:669-681`), driven by the `.reconnecting` connection-state case (`:529-530`). So a rehydrate requires the socket to have visibly dropped to `.reconnecting` first.

2. **App foreground resume while connected** — `handleForegroundResuming` (`:501-523`):
```swift
if latestConnectionState == .connected {
    await rehydrateAfterReconnect(session: session, reason: "Resuming")        // :516-517
} else if latestConnectionState.shouldWaitForForegroundRehydrate {
    markLiveSessionReconnecting("Resuming")                                    // :518-519
```
   Deduped per `snapshot.resumeGeneration` (`:502-505`).

**No periodic poll: CONFIRMED.** The only loop in the file is the pagination `repeat` at `:586`. Grep for `Timer|schedule|interval|asyncAfter|sleep|periodic|poll` in `ThreadDetailStore.swift` returns nothing but that loop. There is no timer that re-drains `thread/turns/list` while the socket merely looks connected. Nothing else triggers rehydrate.

That reframes the whole answer: the canonical methodology is to make existing live-convergence proof *mandatory and ongoing*, not to invent a new framework.

There are also already-existing methodology docs (`CODEX_DOCK_EXHAUSTIVE_SYNC_RUNBOOK`, `CODEX_DOCK_EXHAUSTIVE_SYNC_TEST_PLAN`). I must unify with these, not create a 4th parallel doc. Let me read those owner-path docs directly and fan out two final agents for the drift-gate/CI surface and the full docs landscape.

Use FORCE_LAUNCH=1 to replace it."; exit 0; fi; python3 scripts/sim.py terminate-others "$(SIM)" "$(APP_BUNDLE_ID)"; rtk xcodegen generate --spec project.yml; host_env="$(HOST_ENV_FILE)"; log_dir="$(APP_BUILD_LOG_DIR)"; build_log="$$log_dir/app-sim-build-$(APP_BUILD_NUMBER).log"; install_log="$$log_dir/app-sim-install-$(APP_BUILD_NUMBER).log"; mkdir -p "$$log_dir"; if [ ! 1	# Codex Dock Exhaustive Sync Runbook
2	
3	Date: 2026-05-31
4	Plan: `docs/CODEX_DOCK_EXHAUSTIVE_SYNC_TEST_PLAN_2026-05-31.md`
5	Implementation log:
6	`docs/CODEX_DOCK_EXHAUSTIVE_SYNC_TEST_PLAN_2026-05-31_IMPLEMENTATION_LOG.md`
7	
8	## Purpose
9	
10	Use this runbook to prove the Dock relay and client stay in sync with local
11	Codex state over time. A pass means the client-used relay routes and the
12	literal simulator display receive the data they need, stay current, and do not
13	exceed the configured lag budget.
14	
15	Eventual correctness is not enough. If a row, detail item, request card, stale
16	state, or resolution appears only after the lag budget, the run fails.
17	
18	## Prerequisites
19	
20	Start or reuse the local service stack:
21	
22	```bash
23	rtk make services
24	rtk make app-server-status
25	rtk make dock-relay-status
26	```
27	
28	The normal local relay path is `ws://127.0.0.1:4510` for simulator proof and
29	`ws://<Mac host>:4510` for physical phone proof. Do not point the app at the raw
30	authenticated app-server on `:4500` for completion evidence.
31	
32	Use `/tmp/codex-client/...` for reports. Do not put raw real-home reports in the
33	repo unless they have been intentionally sanitized and reviewed.
34	
35	## Fast Local Checks
36	
37	Run these after relay harness code changes:
38	
39	```bash
40	rtk node --check scripts/dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs
41	rtk node --check scripts/dock-relay-simulator-ui-sync-proof.mjs
42	rtk node --check scripts/dock-relay-controlled-simulator-fixture.mjs
43	rtk node --check scripts/dock-relay-controlled-simulator-matrix.mjs
44	rtk npm run test:relay
45	```
46	
47	Run these after Swift client route, Dock store, or detail-store changes:
48	
49	```bash
50	rtk swift test --filter AppServerClientTests
51	rtk swift test --filter DockStoreTests
52	rtk swift test --filter ThreadDetailStoreTests
53	```
54	
55	If `ThreadDetailStoreTests` times out in an unrelated voice-capture test, record
56	the exact failing test and rerun the exact test. Do not claim broad
57	`ThreadDetailStoreTests` proof until the broad run is clean.
58	
59	## Relay Client-Path Proof
60	
61	One-shot real local proof:
62	
63	```bash
64	rtk node scripts/dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs \
65	  --relay-url ws://127.0.0.1:4510 \
66	  --mode soak \
67	  --duration-ms 0 \
68	  --sample-interval-ms 1 \
69	  --settle-ms 1000 \
70	  --dock-collection-timeout-ms 120000 \
71	  --stream-compare-attempts 5 \
72	  --stream-compare-delay-ms 1000 \
73	  --exhaustive \
74	  --detail sampled \
75	  --detail-limit 1 \
76	  --detail-observe-ms 100 \
77	  --json-out /tmp/codex-client/sync-audit-real-home-exhaustive.json \
78	  --summary-out /tmp/codex-client/sync-audit-real-home-exhaustive.md \
79	  --summary-only \
80	  --fail-on-diff
81	```
82	
83	Over-time client-route soak with forced `dock/resync`:
84	
85	```bash
86	rtk node scripts/dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs \
87	  --relay-url ws://127.0.0.1:4510 \
88	  --mode soak \
89	  --client-path-only \
90	  --force-dock-resync \
91	  --duration-ms 65000 \
92	  --sample-interval-ms 30000 \
93	  --settle-ms 1000 \
94	  --dock-collection-timeout-ms 120000 \
95	  --stream-compare-attempts 5 \
96	  --stream-compare-delay-ms 1000 \
97	  --max-stream-lag-ms 2000 \
98	  --detail sampled \
99	  --detail-limit 5 \
100	  --detail-observe-ms 100 \
101	  --json-out /tmp/codex-client/sync-audit-real-home-client-path-force-resync.json \
102	  --summary-out /tmp/codex-client/sync-audit-real-home-client-path-force-resync.md \
103	  --summary-only \
104	  --fail-on-diff
105	```
106	
107	Required scenario matrix at relay level:
108	
109	```bash
110	rtk node scripts/dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs \
111	  --mode scenario \
112	  --scenario all \
113	  --scenario-repetitions 2 \
114	  --client-path-only \
115	  --detail none \
116	  --dock-collection-timeout-ms 120000 \
117	  --max-stream-lag-ms 2000 \
118	  --json-out /tmp/codex-client/scenario-all-client-path.json \
119	  --summary-out /tmp/codex-client/scenario-all-client-path.md \
120	  --summary-only \
121	  --fail-on-diff
122	```
123	
124	The relay proof must include `initialize`, `initialized`, `dock/subscribe`,
125	`dock/update`, `dock/resync`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, and
126	`thread/resume` where those routes are in scope. Oracle-only routes can explain
127	drift, but they do not prove client delivery.
128	
129	## Simulator Display Proof
130	
131	The completion-grade simulator proof uses the real `iPhone 17` app path. It
132	must start the simulator sampler first, mutate the same relay the app is using,
133	and compare literal displayed UI samples against the relay/client-route report.
134	
135	Run the full controlled simulator matrix twice:
136	
137	```bash
138	rtk make sim-ui-controlled-matrix-proof \
139	  SIM='iPhone 17' \
140	  SIM_UI_CONTROLLED_MATRIX_ROOT=/tmp/codex-client/sim-ui-controlled-matrix-run-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ) \
141	  SIM_UI_CONTROLLED_MATRIX_PASSES=2 \
142	  MAX_UI_LAG_MS=2000 \
143	  SIM_UI_SYNC_CHECKPOINT_SWEEP=1
144	```
145	
146	The default matrix scenarios are:
147	
148	- `detail-history-request`
149	- `large-list-checkpoint`
150	- `thread-activity`
151	- `server-request`
152	- `source-refresh`
153	- `live-lease-expiry`
154	- `multi-host-isolation`
155	- `spawn-edge`
156	- `resync-gap`
157	- `rapid-mutations`
158	
159	The matrix writes one scenario directory per pass under
160	`SIM_UI_CONTROLLED_MATRIX_ROOT`, plus:
161	
162	```text
163	<root>/controlled-simulator-matrix.json
164	<root>/controlled-simulator-matrix.md
165	```
166	
167	Each scenario directory contains:
168	
169	```text
170	relay-client-path.json
171	relay-client-path.md
172	ui-samples.jsonl
173	simulator-ui-sync.json
174	simulator-ui-sync.md
175	controlled-fixture.out.log
176	```
177	
178	For focused debugging, run one scenario:
179	
180	```bash
181	rtk make sim-ui-controlled-scenario-sync-proof \
182	  SIM='iPhone 17' \
183	  SIM_UI_SYNC_SCENARIO=detail-history-request \
184	  SIM_UI_SYNC_DIR=/tmp/codex-client/sim-ui-controlled-detail-history-request-debug \
185	  SIM_UI_SYNC_DURATION_MS=20000 \
186	  SIM_UI_SYNC_SAMPLE_MS=250 \
187	  SIM_UI_SYNC_SCENARIO_HOLD_MS=3500 \
188	  MAX_UI_LAG_MS=2000 \
189	  SIM_UI_SYNC_CHECKPOINT_SWEEP=1 \
190	  SIM_UI_SYNC_READY_TIMEOUT_MS=60000
191	```
192	
193	Use `detail-history-request` when checking opened-thread detail history,
194	request-card visibility, real request action taps, resolved request state, and
195	detail sweep completeness. Use `resync-gap` when checking stream sequence-gap
196	recovery through `dock/resync`.
197	
198	## Matrix Verification Only
199	
200	If scenario reports already exist, verify them without rerunning the simulator:
201	
202	```bash
203	rtk make sim-ui-controlled-matrix-verify \
204	  SIM_UI_MATRIX_REPORT_DIRS='/tmp/codex-client/run/pass-1/detail-history-request /tmp/codex-client/run/pass-1/large-list-checkpoint' \
205	  SIM_UI_MATRIX_MIN_PASSES=1 \
206	  MAX_UI_LAG_MS=2000 \
207	  SIM_UI_MATRIX_JSON=/tmp/codex-client/sim-ui-controlled-matrix.json \
208	  SIM_UI_MATRIX_MD=/tmp/codex-client/sim-ui-controlled-matrix.md
209	```
210	
211	For a completion gate, use `SIM_UI_MATRIX_MIN_PASSES=2` and distinct report
212	directories for each pass. Reusing the same artifact twice is not valid proof.
213	
214	## Physical Phone Proof
215	
216	Physical-phone proof is still required before the whole goal can be called
217	complete. It is not replaced by simulator or local relay proof.
218	
219	Install and configure Amir's iPhone 17 Pro:
220	
221	```bash
222	rtk make iphone-17-pro
223	```
224	
225	Install and configure the iPhone 14:
226	
227	```bash
228	rtk make iphone-14
229	```
230	
231	Verify saved host configs without reinstalling:
232	
233	```bash
234	rtk make device-config-verify DEVICE=CB9FFF0E-89AD-57B5-9C00-6552D814875E
235	rtk make device-config-verify DEVICE=0A4EFF8B-54D8-58FB-B3FB-63263265B9CC
236	```
237	
238	Physical completion evidence must show the installed app connects to the
239	relay-backed host path, renders real `DockThreadCard` rows, and shows
240	offline/error UI when that same host path is unavailable.
241	
242	If physical Mobile MCP reports `WebDriverAgent is not running on device`, stop
243	retrying physical Mobile MCP for that task and record that exact blocker. Use
244	simulator/local proof only for the parts it actually proves.
245	
246	## Reading Results
247	
248	Treat a run as `pass` only when all of these are true:
249	
250	- the command exits 0;
251	- the JSON report has `ok: true`;
252	- `clientPathOK` is true when client-path proof is in scope;
253	- matrix reports show every required scenario passed;
254	- no `streamLagFailures`, `scenarioTransitionFailures`, or
255	  `detailTransitionFailures` are present;
256	- max relay/UI lag is at or below `MAX_UI_LAG_MS`;
257	- checkpoint sweeps and detail sweeps meet the required row counts;
258	- unsupported facts are classified, not hidden.
259	
260	Treat a run as `fail` when the report has missing rows, duplicates, stale data
261	shown as fresh, wrong host/thread/detail identity, skipped transitions, failed
262	request-card visibility/resolution, or lag over budget.
263	
264	Treat a run as `blocked` only when the command could not exercise the intended
265	path because Xcode, a simulator, a physical device, signing, services, or
266	environment variables were unavailable. Record the exact command and exact
267	blocker.
268	
269	Treat a finding as `outside-contract` only when the report explicitly classifies
270	the fact as outside current app-server or client contract. A client-required
271	`product_gap` blocks completion.
272	
273	## CI-Safe Subsets
274	
275	Use these in ordinary local or CI-like checks where no simulator or phone is
276	available:
277	
278	```bash
279	rtk node --check scripts/dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs
280	rtk node --check scripts/dock-relay-simulator-ui-sync-proof.mjs
281	rtk node --check scripts/dock-relay-controlled-simulator-fixture.mjs
282	rtk node --check scripts/dock-relay-controlled-simulator-matrix.mjs
283	rtk npm run test:relay
284	```
285	
286	Use this to validate Makefile wiring without launching a simulator:
287	
288	```bash
289	rtk make -n sim-ui-controlled-matrix-proof \
290	  SIM='iPhone 17' \
291	  SIM_UI_CONTROLLED_MATRIX_PASSES=2 \
292	  MAX_UI_LAG_MS=2000
293	```
294	
295	These CI-safe subsets do not replace the actual `iPhone 17` simulator matrix or
296	physical-phone proof.
297	
298	## Redaction Rules
299	
300	Do not log or publish:
301	
302	- `OPENAI_API_KEY`;
303	- raw app-server bearer tokens;
304	- base64 audio or raw audio bytes;
305	- prompt text;
306	- transcript text;
307	- full JSON-RPC payloads.
308	
309	The harness reports use route counts, ids, statuses, timings, redaction-safe
310	fingerprints, and invariant ids. If a new report includes sensitive data, treat
311	that as a harness failure before sharing the artifact.

2	
3	## Goal
4	
5	Keep one working log for comparing what the iPhone 17 simulator actually shows
6	against the current Codex-backed Dock truth served by the relays.
7	
8	This work log is evidence-first. Do not treat green process health as proof that
9	the phone display is correct. The useful comparison is:
10	
11	1. What the phone/simulator renders.
12	2. What `dock/subscribe` says the current relay-backed Dock card truth is.
13	3. Which client filters or state rules explain any difference.

99	thread `019e7e7d-66ca-7280-9aa0-2e272f1752b1` is rank 1 in relay truth with
100	activity at `2026-05-31T22:03:36.000Z`.

102	The reason it is not visible at the top of the phone screen is the app's
103	default `Idle hidden` filter.
104	
105	The newest relay rows are present but have status `idle`, and Dock is currently
106	hiding idle rows by default. The phone summary proves this: it says `rows=1158`
107	but only `1,153 shown`, so five rows are hidden. The top hidden rows include the
108	fresh current Amir-M5 work.
109	
110	After applying the client's `Idle hidden` rule, the visible phone order matches
111	the filtered relay order:
112	
113	1. Home hill-climb row, status `dormant`.
114	2. Amir-M5 `Find open audit items`, status `dormant`.
115	3. Amir-M5 animation-engine ramp-up, status `dormant`.
116	4. Amir-M5 group-files ramp-up, status `dormant`.
117	
118	### Working Interpretation
119	
120	This is no longer the stale SQLite `orderKey` bug. That was fixed by deleting
121	and rebuilding the relay caches.
122	
123	The remaining user-visible problem is filter/status semantics:
124	
125	- The relay/card truth knows the newest current sessions.
126	- Those newest sessions can be marked `idle`.
127	- The Dock screen defaults to `Idle hidden`.
128	- Therefore current work can be correctly present in Codex and still be hidden
129	from the default phone view.
130	
131	### Open Items

134	- Decide whether a recently active human session should ever be hidden just
135	  because its current runtime status is `idle`.
136	- Fix the repo-owned `sim-ui-sync-proof` path so it produces usable comparison
137	  artifacts when the displayed UI proof fails.

1	# Codex Dock Protocol And Update Architecture Reference
2	
3	Date: 2026-05-31
4	
5	Status: reference plus audit. This document describes the intended architecture,
6	the real update paths in the current repo, the app-server assumptions the relay
7	depends on, and the stale-data failure modes we found while auditing. It does
8	not implement fixes.
9	
10	## Bottom Line
11	
12	Codex Dock has two different update systems:
13	
14	1. Dock and Archive cards are relay-owned streams. The relay polls and
15	   reconciles Codex app-server state into SQLite, then sends `dock/update` or
16	   `archive/update` to subscribed clients.
17	2. Thread Detail is a live forwarded session. The client reads historical turns,
18	   then asks the relay to `thread/resume`; the relay binds that phone WebSocket
19	   to an upstream app-server session and forwards live notifications and server
20	   requests.
21	
22	The current test suite is strong at proving that Swift can apply pre-made
23	snapshots, deltas, and live notifications. It is weaker at proving that real
24	Codex work continues flowing from app-server to relay to phone over time. That
25	gap explains how the app can look connected while a thread or Dock list stops
26	updating.
27	
28	The highest-signal stale-data failures found in this audit are:
29	
30	- Dock can reconnect its WebSocket and re-run `initialize` without re-running
31	  `dock/subscribe`; the stream can look alive but stop receiving card updates.
32	- Thread Detail can miss history after relay-side upstream recovery because the
33	  relay may recover its Mac-side `thread/resume` session without closing the
34	  phone WebSocket; Swift only rehydrates detail when it observes reconnect,
35	  foreground resume, or stream end.
36	- Route health is not data freshness. `/readyz`, `/statusz`, `/routesz`,
37	  `/metricsz`, and `/syncz` can look healthy while cards are stale, partial, or
38	  no longer receiving updates.
39	- Relay subscribe-time buffering protects one race: the relay subscribes before
40	  reading the initial snapshot and buffers newer updates until the snapshot is
41	  returned. That does not protect reconnects that never re-send
42	  `dock/subscribe`.
43	- Most regular tests use fakes or scripted streams. Those tests prove client
44	  merge/render behavior, not the full real app-server -> relay -> iPhone update
45	  path.
46	
47	## Source Audit Inputs
48	
49	This writeup combines parent-agent code reads with six parallel read-only
50	audits covering app-server assumptions, relay state, Swift streams, Thread
51	Detail, tests, and reconnect/freshness failure modes. The parallel outputs were
52	used as evidence inputs; the file paths and code anchors below are the durable
53	reference.
54	
55	## Vocabulary
56	
57	- App-server: the raw Codex local JSON-RPC server, normally on
58	  `ws://127.0.0.1:4500`.
59	- Relay: the Dock relay process, normally on `:4510`. It owns the raw
60	  app-server bearer token and exposes the phone-safe Dock protocol.
61	- Client: the Swift iOS app.
62	- Downstream: relay -> phone/client.
63	- Upstream: relay -> raw Codex app-server.
64	- Snapshot: a full replacement card payload.
65	- Delta: an incremental card payload.
66	- Heartbeat: a stream payload kind Swift can accept, intended to update
67	  freshness without changing rows.
68	- Rehydrate: Thread Detail's full historical refresh:
69	  `thread/read includeTurns:false`, all pages of `thread/turns/list`, then
70	  `thread/resume excludeTurns:true`.
71	- Freshness: whether the relay believes card facts are current.
72	- Completeness: whether the relay believes it has the full relevant set/window.
73	- Live session: a `thread/resume` connection that can forward notifications,
74	  server requests, and turn commands.
75	
76	## Non-Negotiable Architecture Rules
77	
78	1. The phone normally talks to the relay on `:4510`, not directly to raw
79	   app-server on `:4500`.
80	2. Dock Home card truth comes from relay `dock/*` methods, not raw
81	   `thread/list`.
82	3. Archive card truth comes from relay `archive/*` methods.
83	4. Thread Detail history must come from `thread/read includeTurns:false` plus
84	   paged `thread/turns/list`; `thread/resume excludeTurns:true` is only the live
85	   session and compact metadata path.
86	5. The relay, not Swift, owns card recency. Swift renders relay `orderKey` and
87	   must not rebuild card recency from local timestamps.
88	6. `thread/list` order is not a client-visible ordering contract. The relay must
89	   prove card activity with `thread/turns/list` before exposing fresh card
90	   order.
91	7. Route health is not freshness. A route can answer and still return stale or
92	   partial data.
93	8. Local client metadata can decorate rows and pin rows, but it must not create
94	   production thread rows.
95	9. Human-started filtering is intended to be relay-owned, with Swift enforcing a
96	   defensive second filter.
97	10. Any reconnect that changes stream/session identity must force the missing
98	    state to be rebuilt, not merely reconnect a socket.
99	11. A normal phone host config must identify relay hosts only. Saved app configs
100	    are a `hosts` list, and Swift rejects raw app-server port `4500` for normal
101	    app endpoints.
102	
103	## Protocol Surface
104	
105	Swift method constants live in `CodexDock/AppServer/AppServerMethods.swift`.
106	The relay dispatcher that decides what the phone can call lives in
107	`scripts/dock-relay.mjs`.
108	
109	## Forbidden Phone Routes And Side Doors
110	
111	The phone-facing relay dispatcher is an allow-list. Anything not handled in
112	`scripts/dock-relay.mjs` `handleRequest` returns JSON-RPC `-32601`
113	`unsupported method`.
114	
115	Allowed downstream request methods are only:
116	
117	- `initialize`
118	- `dock/subscribe`
119	- `dock/resync`
120	- `archive/subscribe`
121	- `archive/resync`
122	- `thread/read`
123	- `thread/turns/list`
124	- `thread/resume`
125	- `thread/archive`
126	- `thread/unarchive`
127	- `audio/transcription/start`
128	- `audio/transcription/append`
129	- `audio/transcription/commit`
130	- `audio/transcription/cancel`

2795	## Why This Could Be Stuck Without Tests Catching It
2796	
2797	Yes: the current test strategy can miss exactly the kind of bug the user is
2798	seeing.
2799	
2800	The app is mostly about live updates, but many tests are static or scripted:
2801	
2802	- They create a fake stream.
2803	- They hand Swift a snapshot or delta.
2804	- They assert Swift renders or merges it correctly.
2805	
2806	That proves the last step of the pipeline. It does not prove the whole pipeline:
2807	
2808	1. raw Codex app-server notices real current work;
2809	2. relay sees it;
2810	3. relay reconciles it;
2811	4. relay writes correct SQLite card truth;
2812	5. relay publishes `dock/update`;
2813	6. the phone is still subscribed;
2814	7. Swift applies it;
2815	8. UI renders it;
2816	9. tests fail if that does not happen within a real lag budget.
2817	
2818	For Thread Detail, the untested production shape is even more specific:
2819	
2820	1. phone opens detail and resumes live session;
2821	2. relay loses upstream app-server session;
2822	3. relay recovers upstream without closing phone WebSocket;
2823	4. Swift never sees reconnect;
2824	5. Swift never drains `thread/turns/list` again;
2825	6. missed work remains missing.
2826	
2827	That is why "socket connected" and "tests passing" can coexist with "current
2828	work not visible."
2829	
2830	## Testing Strategy Required To Close The Gap
2831	
2832	The required proof should be called live convergence proof, not snapshot proof.
2833	
2834	Proof command matrix:
2835	
2836	| Command / path | What it proves | What it does not prove |
2837	| --- | --- | --- |
2838	| `rtk swift test --filter DockStoreTests` | Swift projection/store behavior against fake/scripted payloads. | Real relay/app-server live convergence. |
2839	| `rtk swift test --filter ThreadDetailStoreTests` | Detail load/merge/reconnect behavior against fake sessions. | Relay-only upstream recovery gaps or real app-server notification coverage. |
2840	| `rtk npm run test:relay` | Relay unit/contract behaviors. | iPhone/simulator UI freshness unless paired with simulator proof. |
2841	| `rtk make app-test SIM='iPhone 17'` | App builds and UI tests selected by the scheme. | Not automatically a live convergence proof unless the specific sync proof test/path is enabled. |
2842	| `CodexDockDisplayedSyncProofTests` | Simulator-visible sampling only when `/tmp/codex-client/codex-dock-sim-ui-sync-config.json` exists and has not expired. | It throws `XCTSkip` without that config, so a skipped default run is not sync proof. |
2843	| `rtk make sim-ui-sync-proof` | Real relay-backed Dock display soak: relay client-path audit runs while the UI sampler records visible rows over time. | Controlled mutation scenarios and physical phone network/Tailscale behavior. |
2844	| `rtk make sim-ui-scenario-sync-proof` | Real relay-backed UI sampler plus relay scenario while the sampler is active. | Fully isolated fake-server control unless using a controlled target. |
2845	| `rtk make sim-ui-controlled-scenario-sync-proof` | Controlled simulator fixture plus displayed UI sampler, suitable for deterministic update/display scenarios. | Real Codex app-server freshness. |
2846	| `rtk make sim-ui-controlled-matrix-proof` | Matrix of controlled simulator display scenarios. | Real Codex app-server and physical phone behavior. |
2847	| `CODEX_DOCK_RUN_ARCHIVE_ROUND_TRIP=1` archive round-trip | Opt-in archive mutation round trip. | Default CI coverage; should not be assumed unless the env var is set. |
2848	
2849	Minimum test tiers:
2850	
2851	### Tier 1: Swift State Tests
2852	
2853	Keep current fake-stream tests. Add missing strictness:
2854	
2855	- reconnect requires stream-level resubscribe or stream failure;
2856	- missing update params are stream corruption, not ignore;
2857	- stale compatible snapshot cannot replace newer state silently;
2858	- normal delta sequence cannot regress;
2859	- non-human upsert for existing human card deletes or resyncs;
2860	- duplicate card ids are rejected safely;
2861	- inconsistent complete windows are rejected;
2862	- upstream `serverRequest/resolved` notification clears existing card;
2863	- reconnect rehydrate with multiple turn pages;
2864	- missing `threadId` in forwarded requests has defined behavior.
2865	
2866	### Tier 2: Relay Contract Tests
2867	
2868	Add relay tests that run a fake app-server plus real relay and assert:
2869	
2870	- subscribe then mutate server state then receive `dock/update`;
2871	- update has valid `baseSeq`, `seq`, `epoch`, and view;
2872	- client-requested `dock/resync` converges after injected gap;
2873	- delete-only deltas work;
2874	- multiple subscribers receive updates;
2875	- archive mutation emits both Dock and Archive changes when appropriate;
2876	- route health marks stale/partial semantic states, or diagnostics clearly show
2877	  freshness separately;
2878	- heartbeat behavior is either emitted and audited or removed from the
2879	  contract.
2880	
2881	### Tier 3: Real Relay Client-Path Soak
2882	
2883	Run `scripts/dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs` or Makefile wrappers against real relay
2884	and real app-server with:
2885	
2886	- long-lived `dock/subscribe`;
2887	- periodic fresh `dock/subscribe`;
2888	- comparison between long-lived stream state and fresh snapshot;
2889	- forced `dock/resync`;
2890	- selected detail probe that runs `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, and
2891	  `thread/resume`;
2892	- lag budget for convergence.
2893	
2894	This is the tier that catches "the stream is stuck while route health is
2895	green."
2896	
2897	### Tier 4: Simulator Display Proof
2898	
2899	Run the controlled simulator proof when UI display behavior matters. It should
2900	verify:
2901	
2902	- real relay-backed rows appear;
2903	- selected row opens detail;
2904	- detail drains `thread/turns/list`;
2905	- detail resumes live session;
2906	- displayed state changes after a controlled update;
2907	- UI exposes stale/partial freshness when the relay says data is stale/partial.
2908	
2909	### Tier 5: Physical Phone Proof
2910	
2911	For phone completion, simulator is not enough. The physical phone path must
2912	prove:
2913	
2914	- installed app connects to relay-backed host path on `:4510`;
2915	- it renders real `DockThreadCard` rows;
2916	- it receives updates after current Codex work changes;
2917	- it shows offline/error/stale UI when the same host path is unavailable.
2918	
2919	## Intended Fix Direction, Not Implementation
2920	
2921	This document is not an implementation plan, but the architecture points to a
2922	small set of design repairs:
2923	
2924	1. Make subscriptions replayable across reconnect, or make AppServerClient
2925	   reconnects terminate stream subscriptions so higher layers reopen and
2926	   resubscribe.
2927	2. Make relay upstream recovery visible to Thread Detail, or force downstream
2928	   reconnect/rehydrate after upstream recovery.
2929	3. Treat freshness/completeness as first-class semantic health, not only route
2930	   success.
2931	4. Align schema, Swift runtime validation, relay emission, and sync audit
2932	   around one stream contract.
2933	5. Make live convergence proof mandatory for update-path changes.

2	import Foundation
3	
4	// Render-only UI fixture. It can exercise controls and layout, but it is not
5	// data-contract proof for freshness, completeness, or card ordering.
6	enum ScriptedDockStreamScenario: String, Sendable {
7	    case retention
8	    case messageNoise
9	    case pinnedOrder
10	    case schemaMismatch
11	}
12	
13	struct ScriptedDockStreamClient: ThreadCardStreamConnecting {
14	    let scenario: ScriptedDockStreamScenario
15	
16	    func connect(to host: DockHostConfiguration) async throws -> any ThreadCardStreamConnection {
17	        ScriptedThreadCardStreamConnection(host: host, scenario: scenario)
18	    }
19	}
20	
21	actor ScriptedThreadCardStreamConnection: ThreadCardStreamConnection {
22	    private let host: DockHostConfiguration
23	    private let scenario: ScriptedDockStreamScenario
24	    private let updateStream: AsyncThrowingStream<ThreadCardStreamUpdateDTO, Error>
25	    private let updateContinuation: AsyncThrowingStream<ThreadCardStreamUpdateDTO, Error>.Continuation
26	    private var updateTask: Task<Void, Never>?
27	
28	    init(host: DockHostConfiguration, scenario: ScriptedDockStreamScenario) {
29	        self.host = host
30	        self.scenario = scenario
31	        let stream = AsyncThrowingStream<ThreadCardStreamUpdateDTO, Error>.makeStream()
32	        self.updateStream = stream.stream
33	        self.updateContinuation = stream.continuation
34	    }
35	
36	    func subscribe() async throws -> ThreadCardStreamUpdateDTO {
37	        DockLog.dock.notice("dock stream subscribe started host_id=\(self.host.id, privacy: .public) scripted_scenario=\(self.scenario.rawValue, privacy: .public)")
38	        startScriptIfNeeded()
39	        let snapshot = snapshot(seq: 1, freshness: .fresh, cards: initialCards())
40	        DockLog.dock.notice("dock stream subscribe finished host_id=\(self.host.id, privacy: .public) seq=\(snapshot.seq, privacy: .public) scripted_scenario=\(self.scenario.rawValue, privacy: .public)")
41	        return snapshot
42	    }
43	
44	    func resync() async throws -> ThreadCardStreamUpdateDTO {
45	        let snapshot = snapshot(seq: 4, freshness: .fresh, cards: resyncedCards())
46	        DockLog.dock.notice("dock stream scripted resync finished host_id=\(self.host.id, privacy: .public) seq=\(snapshot.seq, privacy: .public) rows=\(snapshot.cards?.count ?? 0, privacy: .public)")
47	        return snapshot
48	    }
49	
50	    nonisolated func updates() -> AsyncThrowingStream<ThreadCardStreamUpdateDTO, Error> {
51	        updateStream
52	    }
53	
54	    func close() async {
55	        updateTask?.cancel()
56	        updateTask = nil
57	        updateContinuation.finish()
58	    }
59	
60	    private func startScriptIfNeeded() {
61	        guard updateTask == nil else {
62	            return
63	        }
64	        updateTask = Task { [weak self] in
65	            await self?.runScript()
66	        }
67	    }
68	
69	    private func runScript() async {
70	        switch scenario {
71	        case .retention:
72	            await runRetentionScript()
73	        case .messageNoise:
74	            await runMessageNoiseScript()
75	        case .pinnedOrder:
76	            await runPinnedOrderScript()
77	        case .schemaMismatch:
78	            await runSchemaMismatchScript()
79	        }
80	    }
81	
82	    private func runRetentionScript() async {
83	        await sleep(milliseconds: 250)
84	        yield(heartbeat(seq: 1, freshness: .fresh))
85

402	        // card contract. Rows expected to be visible must obey the same
403	        // human-lane policy as production relay card streams.

437	    private func iso8601(seq: Int64) -> String {
438	        let date = Date(timeIntervalSince1970: TimeInterval(1_779_990_000 + seq))

440	    }

443	        let date = Date(timeIntervalSince1970: TimeInterval(timestamp))

1	# Codex Dock Exhaustive Sync Test Plan
2	
3	> 2026-05-31 implementation note: this draft references older parity/oracle
4	> routes as historical context. Current card proof must observe `dock/subscribe`,
5	> `dock/update`, `dock/resync`, `archive/subscribe`, `archive/update`, and
6	> `archive/resync`. Deleted routes such as `relay/state/snapshot`, `state/query`,
7	> `thread/search`, `thread/goal/get`, app-facing `thread/loaded/list`, `/statez`,
8	> `/dbz`, and `/explainz` must not be reintroduced as test-only or diagnostic
9	> card proof paths.
10	
11	Date: 2026-05-31
12	Status: Draft for audit
13	Doc type: Implementation plan
14	Owners: Amir, Codex
15	
16	Related docs:
17	
18	- `README.md`
19	- `docs/CODEX_DOCK_EXHAUSTIVE_SYNC_RUNBOOK_2026-05-31.md`
20	- `docs/CODEX_DISK_DB_THREAD_TYPES_AND_STATE_2026-05-29.md`
21	- `docs/CODEX_APP_SERVER_THREAD_TYPES_AND_STATE_2026-05-29.md`
22	- `docs/CODEX_DOCK_CODEX_APP_SERVER_END_TO_END_AUDIT.md`
23	- `docs/CODEX_DOCK_RELAY_STATE_PARITY_WORKLOG_2026-05-30.md`
24	
25	## Direct Answer
26	
27	The repo already has a strong one-shot parity foundation in
28	`scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs`, but it does not yet prove that the Dock
29	client stays in sync with the actual local Codex state over time.
30	
31	The missing piece is a long-running sync harness that keeps the Dock stream open,
32	clicks through or protocol-loads thread detail, watches real changes happen, and
33	compares all client-visible state back to local Codex storage and app-server
34	state on every pass.
35	
36	Eventual sync is not enough. If client-visible state catches up only after a
37	noticeable delay, the exhaustive plan must treat that as a failure because the
38	installed client feels stale while the lag is happening.
39	
40	This document specifies that harness and the ongoing loop. It is a plan only.
41	No implementation is included in this document.
42	
43	## Goal
44	
45	Build a repeatable sync-test mechanism that proves Codex Dock stays aligned with
46	the actual local Codex instance over time and stays close enough to real time
47	that user-visible lag is not hidden as a passing result.
48	
49	The mechanism must cover both client surfaces:
50	
51	1. The Dock/Home list: the cards, ordering, archive membership, source grouping,
52	   live status, goals, and host identity shown before opening a thread.
53	2. The click-through thread detail: the exact thread opened from a Dock row, its
54	   metadata, all historical turns, live events, server request cards, reconnect
55	   behavior, and stale/error states.
56	
57	The final proof has three legs:
58	
59	1. Codex storage and app-server truth to relay projection.
60	2. Relay projection to actual client-exercised protocol routes.
61	3. Actual simulator client display, using the `iPhone 17` simulator, so the
62	   test proves what is literally visible in the app stays complete, correct, and
63	   close to real time over time.
64	
65	The third leg is mandatory, not optional follow-up work. After the
66	Codex-to-relay path and relay-to-client-route path are green, the work must
67	continue through the real simulator client display before this goal is called
68	done. A result is not complete if the app screen is missing data, showing stale
69	data, showing the wrong row/detail state, or showing the right data only after a
70	lag the user can feel.
71	
72	Before the goal can be called complete, a passing first and second leg must
73	roll directly into the third simulator-display leg. A relay/client-route pass is
74	not enough if the actual app screen can still miss data, show stale data, or
75	lag beyond the client-visible budget.
76	
77	The mechanism must compare four planes of truth:
78	
79	1. Local Codex durable storage under `CODEX_HOME`, including SQLite metadata,
80	   rollout JSONL session files, archived session files, goals, and spawn edges.
81	2. Raw Codex app-server behavior exposed through relay-side app-server calls,
82	   including `thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`,
83	   `thread/goal/get`, `thread/loaded/list`, notifications, and server requests.
84	3. Dock relay projection behavior, including the relay SQLite projection,
85	   `dock/subscribe`, `dock/update`, `dock/resync`, reconciliation freshness,
86	   windowing, and stale-scope handling.
87	4. Swift client state and rendered simulator UI, including `DockStore`,
88	   `AppServerThreadCardStreamClient`, `ThreadDetailStore`,
89	   `ThreadDetailDataEngine`, visible `DockThreadCard` rows, detail content,
90	   stale/error states, and literal screen proof when required.
91	
92	## Non-Goals
93	
94	- Do not implement the harness in this plan.
95	- Do not make the iPhone connect directly to the raw authenticated
96	  `ws://127.0.0.1:4500` app-server for normal proof.
97	- Do not add relay runtime reads from Codex disk as a production shortcut.
98	  Disk reads are allowed for the verifier oracle only.
99	- Do not use preview rows, mocks, or scripted transports as completion evidence
100	  for physical or installed-client behavior.
101	- Do not log `OPENAI_API_KEY`, bearer tokens, base64 audio, raw audio bytes,
102	  prompt text, transcript text, or full JSON-RPC payloads.
103	- Do not claim unsupported Codex facts are verified. Unsupported facts must be
104	  named as product-contract gaps or app-server gaps.
105	
106	## Current State
107	
108	As of the 2026-05-31 single-source contract cleanup, card proof must run through
109	the same client path the app renders: `dock/subscribe`, `dock/update`, and
110	`dock/resync`. The deleted oracle routes `relay/state/snapshot`, `state/query`,
111	`thread/search`, `thread/goal/get`, and `thread/loaded/list` must not return as
112	app-facing or test-only card proof paths.
113	
114	The remaining relay sync audit is client-path-only. It may use raw Codex facts
115	as upstream fixture/verifier inputs, but the observed relay output for Dock
116	cards is the Dock stream contract.
117	That foundation still needs over-time proof for these behaviors:
118	
119	- A long-lived `dock/subscribe` stream stays correct across many
120	  reconciliations.
121	- `dock/update` deltas stay gap-free and are correctly resynced after sequence
122	  breaks.
123	- Relay stale rows are retained only while a source refresh is incomplete and
124	  removed after a complete refresh proves they are gone.
125	- Swift `DockStore` state keeps matching the relay projection across many
126	  updates.
127	- A real Dock row click opens the exact matching thread detail.
128	- The detail store cannot drop live events between historical read, turn
129	  pagination, and `thread/resume`.
130	- Server requests that matter to the user are visible as both timeline events
131	  and request cards.
132	- Reconnect and foreground rehydrate restore truth before declaring `.live`.
133	
134	## Existing Architecture Evidence

945	## Ongoing Test Loop
946	
947	The ongoing process is the real answer to the over-time question. The team
948	should not rely on a single parity command.
949	
950	### Preflight
951	
952	Run the canonical services:
953	
954	```bash
955	rtk make services
956	```
957	
958	Check service state:
959	
960	```bash
961	rtk make app-server-status
962	rtk make dock-relay-status
963	```
964	
965	If service checks fail, stop the sync audit and record the exact failing command
966	and blocker.
967	
968	### Baseline One-Shot
969	
970	Run the exhaustive one-shot audit:
971	
972	```bash
973	rtk node scripts/dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs \
974	  --relay-url ws://127.0.0.1:4510 \
975	  --mode one-shot \
976	  --exhaustive \
977	  --detail sampled \
978	  --fail-on-diff
979	```
980	
981	Purpose:
982	
983	- prove the current state is not already divergent;
984	- discover unsupported fields before the soak starts;
985	- choose detail targets from real Dock rows.
986	
987	During migration from the current parity tool, also run the existing baseline:
988	
989	```bash
990	rtk node scripts/dock-relay-state-parity.mjs \
991	  --relay-url ws://127.0.0.1:4510 \
992	  --exhaustive \
993	  --fail-on-diff
994	```
995	
996	Purpose:
997	
998	- prove the new tool has not weakened today's one-shot parity coverage;
999	- keep `dock-relay-state-parity.mjs` useful until the shared collectors fully
1000	  replace duplicate one-shot logic.
1001	
1002	### Soak Run
1003	
1004	Run the long-lived stream audit:
1005	
1006	```bash
1007	rtk node scripts/dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs \
1008	  --relay-url ws://127.0.0.1:4510 \
1009	  --mode soak \
1010	  --duration-ms 900000 \
1011	  --sample-interval-ms 30000 \
1012	  --exhaustive \
1013	  --detail sampled \
1014	  --fail-on-diff
1015	```
1016	
1017	Purpose:
1018	
1019	- keep `dock/subscribe` open;
1020	- observe `dock/update` over many reconciliation intervals;
1021	- compare every sample to fresh app-server and storage truth;
1022	- open detail for selected rows during the run;
1023	- verify reconnect and resync paths when injected or naturally triggered.
1024	
1025	### Controlled Scenario Run
1026	
1027	Run isolated scenarios in a temporary Codex home:
1028	
1029	```bash
1030	rtk node scripts/dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs \
1031	  --mode scenario \
1032	  --scenario all \
1033	  --codex-home /tmp/codex-client/sync-audit/codex-home \
1034	  --relay-url ws://127.0.0.1:4510 \
1035	  --exhaustive \
1036	  --detail all \
1037	  --fail-on-diff
1038	```
1039	
1040	Purpose:
1041	
1042	- prove known transitions, not only whatever happens to exist in the user's
1043	  personal Codex home;
1044	- produce deterministic failure cases;
1045	- test archive, unarchive, live lease expiry, server requests, reconnect, and
1046	  resync.
1047	
1048	### Swift Client Proof
1049	
1050	For Swift store changes or final client confidence, run the smallest relevant
1051	tests first:
1052	
1053	```bash
1054	rtk swift test --filter DockStoreTests
1055	rtk swift test --filter ThreadDetailStoreTests
1056	rtk swift test --filter AppServerClientTests
1057	```
1058	
1059	For installed simulator UI behavior:
1060	
1061	```bash
1062	rtk make app-test SIM='iPhone 17'
1063	```

1389	### Phase 7: Runbook And Continuous Loop
1390	
1391	Goal: make the harness usable repeatedly.
1392	
1393	Tasks:
1394	
1395	- Document the one-shot, soak, scenario, Swift proof, and simulator displayed-UI
1396	  proof commands in `README.md` or a dedicated runbook.
1397	- Define where reports go under `/tmp/codex-client/...`.
1398	- Add CI-safe subsets if possible.
1399	- Keep real-home audits local-only unless sanitized report artifacts are
1400	  intentionally shared.
1401	
1402	Exit criteria:
1403	
1404	- A developer can run the loop without reading source code.
1405	- The loop clearly says pass, fail, blocked, or outside-contract.
1406	- Reports preserve exact commands and exact blockers.
1407	
1408	## Completion Gate
1409	
1410	The mechanism is complete only when all of these are true:
1411	
1412	1. One-shot audit passes on a real local service stack.
1413	2. Soak audit passes across multiple reconciliation intervals.
1414	3. Controlled scenario audit passes for required transitions.
1415	4. Dock stream proof includes `dock/subscribe`, `dock/update`, and
1416	   `dock/resync`.

content.content:
1	✅ My recommendation: make the relay the only production data owner, and make every live subscription/session rebuild itself whenever its identity changes. A socket being “connected” must never count as proof that Dock cards or Thread Detail are fresh.
2	
3	**Proposed Architecture**
4	1. Phone talks only to Dock relay `:4510`; raw app-server `:4500` stays Mac-side.
5	2. Dock and Archive card truth comes only from relay `dock/*` and `archive/*`.
6	3. Relay owns card freshness, completeness, order, human filtering, and SQLite projection.
7	4. Swift renders relay `orderKey`; local metadata can only decorate rows.
8	5. Thread Detail always follows one path: `thread/read includeTurns:false` → full paged `thread/turns/list` → `thread/resume excludeTurns:true`.
9	6. No silent reconnects for stateful paths. If Dock, Archive, or Detail loses a stream/session generation, the missing state must be rebuilt.
10	7. For Thread Detail, the leanest rule is: if relay loses and recovers the upstream `thread/resume` session, close the downstream phone socket unless app-server gives a proven replay guarantee. Swift already knows how to rehydrate after a visible reconnect.
11	
12	**Ongoing Test Method**
13	Use five tiers, and do not let lower tiers replace higher tiers:
14	
15	1. Contract checks: `rtk npm run contract:check`, plus drift checks tying schema, Swift DTOs, relay allow-list, and docs together.
16	2. Swift unit tests: keep fake-stream tests for merge, resync, pagination, request cards, stale UI, and edge cases.
17	3. Relay integration tests: fake app-server + real relay, proving real `dock/update`, `archive/update`, `dock/resync`, multi-subscriber, delete-only delta, archive mutation, and upstream recovery behavior.
18	4. Real relay soak: `scripts/dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs` must compare long-lived stream state against fresh client-path snapshots over time and fail on lag over budget.
19	5. Simulator/phone proof: `rtk make sim-ui-controlled-matrix-proof SIM='iPhone 17' ... SIM_UI_CONTROLLED_MATRIX_PASSES=2 MAX_UI_LAG_MS=2000`, then physical phone proof when claiming phone completion.
20	
21	**Owner Paths**
22	- Card contract: `contract/dock/dock-thread-card.schema.json`, `scripts/generate-dock-thread-card-contract.mjs`, `scripts/check-dock-thread-card-contract.mjs`.
23	- Relay route allow-list: `scripts/dock-relay.mjs`.
24	- Swift route names: `CodexDock/AppServer/AppServerMethods.swift`.
25	- Relay card truth: `scripts/dock-relay-state-engine.mjs`, `scripts/dock-relay-state-subscriptions.mjs`, `scripts/dock-relay-state-store.mjs`.
26	- Dock client: `CodexDock/State/AppServerThreadCardStreamClient.swift`, `CodexDock/State/DockStore.swift`, `CodexDock/State/ThreadCardTable.swift`.
27	- Detail client: `CodexDock/State/ThreadDetailStore.swift`, `CodexDock/State/AppServerThreadDetailSession.swift`, `CodexDock/ThreadDetail/ThreadDetailDataEngine.swift`.
28	- Proof harness: `scripts/dock-relay-sync-audit.mjs`, `scripts/dock-relay-controlled-simulator-fixture.mjs`, `scripts/dock-relay-controlled-simulator-matrix.mjs`, `CodexDockUITests/CodexDockDisplayedSyncProofTests.swift`, `Makefile`.
29	
30	**Edge Cases To Require**
31	- Silent WebSocket reconnect without `dock/subscribe`.
32	- Relay upstream detail recovery with phone socket still open.
33	- Cold, empty, stale, or partial SQLite cache.
34	- Raw app-server down while relay process is up.
35	- Sequence gap, schema mismatch, epoch mismatch, large snapshot fallback.
36	- Partial windows and catch-up restart.
37	- Duplicate card IDs, missing `dock/update` params, stale compatible snapshots.
38	- Non-human row replacing an existing human row.
39	- Archive/unarchive updating both Dock and Archive views.
40	- Multi-host alias collisions.
41	- Repeated turn cursors, compact resume payloads, missing `threadId`, unknown live events.
42	- Server request stale generation and request-card resolution.
43	- Background/foreground rehydrate.
44	- `itemsView:"full"` for detail turn history, if app-server supports that enum.
45	
46	**Side Doors To Close**
47	- Swift must not call phone-side `thread/list`, `thread/loaded/list`, `thread/search`, or `relay/state/*`.
48	- `/readyz`, `/statusz`, `/routesz`, `/metricsz`, and `/syncz` are diagnostics, not freshness proof.
49	- `CODEX_DOCK_UI_DOCK_STREAM_SCENARIO` is fixture-only and cannot count as live proof.
50	- One-shot host tests cannot prove Dock Home’s existing stream.
51	- Local metadata cannot create rows or change freshness/order.
52	- Preview rows and static fixtures cannot be production evidence.
53	- Phone must not connect to raw `:4500`.
54	
55	**Rejected Alternatives**
56	- Relying on snapshots/fixtures: catches merge bugs, misses over-time delivery bugs.
57	- Letting Swift infer recency from timestamps: creates a second card-truth path.
58	- Treating route health as data health: route success can coexist with stale cards.
59	- Adding a second relay state oracle route: creates drift beside `dock/*` and `archive/*`.
60	- Keeping detail upstream recovery invisible: this is the exact stale-detail failure shape.
61	
62	**Documentation Deliverable Shape**
63	Create a new doc, likely:
64	`docs/CODEX_DOCK_LIVE_UPDATE_ARCHITECTURE_AND_TESTING_REFERENCE_2026-06-01.md`
65	
66	Keep it shorter than the audit doc and structure it as:

94	Simulator, local relay, service-status, and generated-artifact proof only prove
95	the parts they actually exercise.
96	
97	## Exhaustive Sync Harness
98	
99	The repeatable over-time sync proof is documented in
100	`docs/CODEX_DOCK_EXHAUSTIVE_SYNC_RUNBOOK_2026-05-31.md`.
101	
102	Use it when checking whether Codex storage, app-server state, relay projection,
103	client-used routes, and the literal `iPhone 17` simulator display stay in sync.
104	The harness treats lag over the configured budget as a failure, even if a later
105	sample eventually catches up.
106	
107	## Canonical Service Start
108	
109	Use this target for local Dock development instead of manually starting and
110	stopping host services:
111	
112	```sh
113	rtk make services
114	```
115	
116	It starts/reuses two real services and leaves them running:
117	
118	- Raw Codex app-server on loopback `ws://127.0.0.1:4500`
119	- Dock relay on `ws://<APP_SERVER_HOST>:4510`
120	
121	The raw app-server provides stored history. The relay is the app endpoint. Dock
122	Home subscribes to relay-owned `dock/*` methods: `dock/subscribe` returns the
123	first normalized snapshot, `dock/update` pushes deltas and heartbeats, and
124	`dock/resync` returns a replacement snapshot if the client detects a sequence
125	gap. The relay materializes app-server thread projections in SQLite at
126	`.codex-dock/relay-state.sqlite`, serves Dock Home from that state store, and
127	keeps stale rows visible when a source refresh fails.
128	
129	Card truth has one path. The relay may inspect raw app-server facts such as
130	`thread/list`, `thread/read`, `thread/turns/list`, live events, and live loaded
131	IDs internally, but Swift never uses those raw routes to prove Dock or Archive
132	cards. Swift renders card truth only from `dock/*` and `archive/*` streams.
133	
134	Row text has two separate meanings. Raw history `preview` is preserved as the
135	app-server's stored preview and may be the opening message. Dock overview rows
136	use relay-owned card fields from the canonical projection. That projection may
137	inspect newest turns and live events to compute honest activity, but any
138	unproven card makes the stream partial or stale instead of pretending the list
139	is fresh.
140	
141	The relay also owns OpenAI Realtime transcription. Keep `OPENAI_API_KEY` in the
142	Mac environment or repo `.env`; the app never receives it. The default Realtime
143	transcription model is `gpt-realtime-whisper`, with optional Mac-side
144	`CODEX_DOCK_OPENAI_REALTIME_TRANSCRIPTION_MODEL` and
145	`CODEX_DOCK_REALTIME_TRANSCRIPTION_DELAY` overrides.
146	
147	The Dock filters loaded thread cards locally. It opens to `Newest`: one flat
148	newest-first list across configured hosts. Rows carry their own short host
149	name, repository or working directory, branch, status, last activity, local
150	label, and latest summary. `Host` and `Branch` are Dock lenses, not app-level
151	tabs or a separate sort picker; both preserve newest-first ordering inside
152	their groups. `Filters` opens one shared filter surface for host, branch,
153	canonical Dock status, repository or working directory, source, and the fixed
154	`Newest activity` sort. Status `Any` includes `Idle`, so idle rows are visible
155	by default and can be narrowed through the status filter. Search is full-width and
156	matches session title, label, repository or working directory, branch, summary,
157	status, host display name, host id, source, and thread id. Codex runtime
158	`notLoaded` is normalized by the relay to Dock `dormant`; Dock Home does not
159	spend row-badge space on that background state.
160	
161	The app has one root connectivity indicator. It appears above Dock and opens
162	the `System Health` sheet for relay and route diagnostics. Archive recovery,
163	cleanup, and relay host editing live in the Dock `More` menu as `Archived
164	Threads`, `Archive Cleanup`, and `Relay Settings` task sheets, not app-level
165	tabs. The labels are `Unconfigured`,
166	`Checking`, `Online`, `Partial`, `Reconnecting`, `Backgrounded`, `Resuming`,
167	`Stale`, `Offline`, `Error`, and `Config error`. A nil host bearer token is
168	normal for the personal physical-phone relay path; it is not shown as missing
169	credentials.
170	
171	Live Session detail connections reconnect automatically when recovery is safe.
172	After reconnect, the app re-runs the full detail rehydrate path:
173	`thread/read includeTurns:false`, paged `thread/turns/list` until `nextCursor`
174	is exhausted, and `thread/resume excludeTurns:true`. The turn-list page size is
175	a transport guard, not a total message cap. Failed user sends are not silently
176	replayed. If the relay loses its upstream session, it either re-resumes upstream
177	or closes the phone WebSocket so Swift can mark the detail stale or reconnect.
178	
179	When iOS backgrounds the app, root refresh and reconnect attempts pause instead
180	of spending retry budget. Open details keep visible events, request action
181	state, and draft text but are no longer labeled fresh. Active voice capture is
182	cancelled without auto-submitting. On foreground resume, Dock and Archive
183	refresh from root, open details rehydrate through the same full detail path, and
184	the indicator moves through `Backgrounded` / `Resuming` / `Reconnecting` as
185	appropriate.
186	
187	The service targets install per-repo launchd files on macOS and systemd user
188	files on Linux, with runtime files under `.codex-dock/`:

# Codex Dock Data Contract Single Source Implementation Plan - 2026-05-31

## Bottom Line

The intended user experience is simple: Dock and Archive show the work that most
recently happened, newest first. Manual pins may keep a thread visible, but pins
must not invent recency, status, title, summary, freshness, or activity.

The implementation pattern is also simple: one relay projection owns all card
truth. Swift renders `dock/*` and `archive/*` card streams. Every other route,
diagnostic, script, fixture, command, and local cache is explicitly scoped so it
cannot become a second source of Dock or Archive card truth.

Related audit: [Codex Dock Relay Data Contract And Lease Drift Audit](CODEX_DOCK_RELAY_DATA_CONTRACT_AND_LEASE_DRIFT_AUDIT_2026-05-31.md).

# Codex Dock Staleness Architecture Root Cause Report - 2026-05-31

## Bottom line

The simulator and phone can look online while showing stale Dock data because the architecture treats transport health and data freshness as separate things, then the client UI rolls stale Dock freshness up as `partial`, and `partial` counts as online-like.

That is the architectural bug: a stale retained list is not elevated to a first-class stale app state. It is allowed to keep rendering cached rows under a global badge that can say `Online 2/2`.

No implementation fix was made in this investigation.
